Admin responses never CDN-cached, no cross-merchant cache bleed - verified live: /api/admin/* returns Cache-Control: no-store, X-Vercel-Cache: BYPASS; cache keys include full path+query. Security headers (HSTS 2y preload, nosniff, frame-deny, Referrer-Policy) present on all responses; no permissive CORS (no ACAO header returned to Origin: evil.example).

findings.title: Operator/Control Center surface has no real authentication (self-mintable ops token behind a fake OTP login)
findings.evidence: Live: `curl -s -X POST https://zarbin-nine.vercel.app/api/auth/session?scope=ops` returns a valid ops token to an anonymous caller; presenting it, `GET /api/admin/platform` -> 200 with platform-wide data (343 merchants, gmv 5,165,464,690,799), while no token -> 403. auth_session mints scope=ops unconditionally (no credential). Login.tsx OTP submit performs no verification - it just calls auth/session and onLogin(target); the 5-digit code is never checked. So the whole operator surface is public behind a UI that fakes authentication.
findings.impact: Anyone on the internet can read the entire operator surface (platform metrics, per-merchant rankings/GMV, AI-ops cost, data-source status). Data is anonymized aggregates (no PII/cards/secrets), and memory.md documents 'no auth/RBAC enforced' as a demo posture, so this is an intentional single-tenant demo rather than a data breach - but the OTP screen misrepresents that no access control exists.
findings.fix: Gate scope=ops minting behind a real credential (server-side OTP/operator secret) before any public deploy, or set ZARIN_ADMIN_TOKEN so /api/admin/* requires X-Admin-Token; make the frontend OTP actually verify server-side.

findings.title: No rate limiting on any endpoint; unauthenticated path drives real external LLM calls
findings.evidence: Live: 15 rapid `GET /api/copilot/polish?m=M156&q=...` with no auth all returned 200. /api/admin/ai-ops shows llm_requests:1, model nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free - i.e. OPENROUTER_API_KEY is live and polish can reach OpenRouter. polish is public (no auth) and each call can trigger an external round trip (OPENROUTER_TIMEOUT=20s) inside a maxDuration=60s function.
findings.impact: An anonymous attacker can drive unbounded external LLM calls (draining OpenRouter free-tier quota -> polish degrades platform-wide) and unbounded Vercel function invocations (availability/cost abuse). No direct billing risk because models are :free, but it is a resource/quota-exhaustion vector with no throttle anywhere.
findings.fix: Add per-IP rate limiting (edge middleware or a token-bucket in cache.py) to /api/copilot* and the admin/auth routes; cap concurrent polish calls.

findings.title: No Content-Security-Policy header on the SPA
findings.evidence: `curl -s -i https://zarbin-nine.vercel.app/` returns Referrer-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, HSTS but no Content-Security-Policy. Verified no CSP on API or HTML responses.
findings.impact: Defense-in-depth gap for an app that renders LLM-influenced Persian text. React auto-escaping and the grounding guard (which blocks injected links/scripts in copilot output) make practical XSS unlikely, so impact is limited, but a strict CSP would harden the SPA against any future injection sink.
findings.fix: Add a Content-Security-Policy header (default-src 'self'; the app is self-contained except Google Fonts if used) to the vercel.json /(.*) headers block.

findings.title: Shipped tenant-isolation auth is inert in production (REQUIRE_AUTH off)
findings.evidence: Live: `GET /api/overview?m=M18` (or any merchant) returns full data with no token, because REQUIRE_AUTH is off, so _merchant_scope returns the client-supplied m verbatim. The whole merchant API is public.
findings.impact: Any merchant's aggregate data is readable by anyone via ?m=. This is documented and the challenge brief explicitly calls the merchant API public, so it is intended - but the elaborate auth.py/_merchant_scope tenant scoping is not actually enforced on the live system. Flagged for completeness.
findings.fix: For a real multi-tenant deploy set ZARIN_REQUIRE_AUTH=1 and derive m from the verified session token instead of the query param (the code already supports this).

lenses.summary: I fired ~90 hostile probes at the live deployment (malformed/reversed/out-of-range dates, 501- and 10 000-char questions, NUL bytes, RLO overrides, emoji, Arabic yeh/kaf, ZWNJ, SQL and HTML payloads, limit=-5/0/999999999, unknown merchants, 7 path-traversal spellings, 6 token-tamper variants, a 24-way concurrent burst) and could not produce a single 500 from outside: the boundary validation is real and returns the offending value plus the expected format. The observability, however, is not trustworthy. Three of the product's own health numbers are quantifiably wrong in the optimistic direction: I reproduced an AI-Ops panel reporting fallback_rate 0.08 and p95 900 ms when the truth was 8 rejections in 10 LLM calls at 17 000 ms (10x and 19x understated), and the live deployment shows the same signature (fallback=14 with llm_requests=3). `Server-Timing: app;dur` — the header the product tells clients to trust — came back frozen at 302.9 ms with `Age: 121` on a CDN hit, and on 20 all-MISS concurrent requests read 61 ms p50 against 3103 ms wall. The request-telemetry ring silently reset from total=267 to total=7 mid-session with no indication, and 3000 anonymous `/api/<random>` requests produced 3001 endpoint rows and a 389 KB operator response while `attention` stayed empty at a 99.97% client-error rate. Worst: with `ZARIN_REQUIRE_AUTH=1` — the documented production mode and the recorded fix for ZB-001/ZB-030, both marked ✅ fixed — the response cache answers before the auth dependency, returning M18's 968 621 609 500 IRR GMV to an M156-scoped token under `Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=31536000`.
lenses.not_higher_because: Three independent health metrics on the operator surface are measurably wrong in the flattering direction (AI fallback rate 10x low, AI p95 19x low, request p50 ~50x below user-observed latency), an anonymous caller can evict the telemetry ring and inflate the operator response 200x, and the tenancy fix recorded as ✅ fixed is bypassable by the process's own cache. A production fintech cannot ship an AI-health panel that reads 8% when the measured truth is 80%, nor an "attention" rule that stays silent while 99.97% of requests fail.
lenses.not_lower_because: The trust boundary itself is genuinely well built: ~90 malformed/hostile inputs produced zero server errors, every rejection named the offending value and the expected form (`invalid date for f: 'banana' (expected YYYY-MM-DD)`, `question too long (max 500 chars)`, `Input should be less than or equal to 50`), path traversal in 7 spellings served the SPA index, all 6 token-tamper variants returned an identical non-leaking 403, and 24 concurrent uncached requests all returned 200 at 165 ms app p95. ZB-021's fix works — I forced a 500 and obs recorded error_rate 1.0 and raised a high-severity Persian attention item naming the path. 20 parallel cross-instance admin calls all succeeded, proving `ZARIN_SESSION_SECRET` is really set as the deploy invariant demands. None of the auth-cache damage is reachable on the deployed configuration today.
verified_strengths: ZB-021's fix is real, not just recorded as fixed: I monkeypatched analytics.overview to raise, and obs.summary() came back with error_rate 1.0 plus a correctly-worded high-severity attention item naming the path in Persian — the exception path genuinely reaches the telemetry ring through the cache middleware sitting between it and the route.

Boundary validation survives sustained abuse: across ~90 hostile live probes (f=banana, f=2026-13-45, limit=-5/0/abc/999999999, outcome=DROP, m='' OR 1=1--, empty f1/t1, missing required params) I could not produce a single 5xx, and each rejection echoed the offending value with the expected form (`invalid date for f: 'banana' (expected YYYY-MM-DD)`, `Input should be less than or equal to 50`, `unknown outcome: 'DROP'`). The basic-ISO normalisation the team added is live: f1=20260101 and f1=2026-W01-1 both return 200 instead of the DuckDB 500 they used to.

Unicode robustness is genuinely solid, which matters for a Persian RTL product: 15 payloads through /api/copilot — 10 KB of Persian, emoji, U+202E RLO override, an embedded NUL byte, raw newlines/tabs, Arabic yeh and kaf, Arabic-Indic digits, ZWNJ-shredded words, <script> and a SQL DROP string — all returned 200 with a correctly-routed or correctly-refused Persian answer, and the 500-char cap fired at exactly 501 (`{"detail":"question too long (max 500 chars)"}`).

Token verification is textbook and I could not weaken it: no header, `Bearer zzz`, a truncated token, a signature with the last 4 bytes replaced, a merchant-scope token on an ops route, and the token without the `Bearer ` prefix all returned an identical `403 {"detail":"ops session required"}` with no oracle. auth.py uses hmac.compare_digest, rejects iat more than 300 s in the future, and enforces a 12 h max age.

The deploy invariants hold under real conditions: 20 parallel /api/admin/platform calls with one token all returned 200 across multiple lambda instances, proving ZARIN_SESSION_SECRET is actually set (memory.md warns tokens "break at random" otherwise); a 24-way concurrent burst of uncached /api/overview queries returned 24/24 200s at app p95 165 ms; and 7 path-traversal spellings (/api/../../etc/passwd, /assets/../../zarin/config.py, /%c0%ae%c0%ae/) all served the SPA index rather than a file.

findings.title: Response cache answers merchant routes before the auth dependency, leaking another tenant's money (defeats the recorded ZB-001/ZB-030 fix)
findings.location: zarin/cache.py:92-100 (middleware) vs zarin/api.py:36-37 (registration order) and zarin/api.py:121 (_merchant_scope)
findings.evidence:
docs/EXPERT_REVIEW.md:335 and :364 record ZB-001 and ZB-030 as "✅ fixed". They are not, in the mode the fix exists for. Repro at pipeline/_panel/rel_authcache.py with ZARIN_REQUIRE_AUTH=1:
  1 no-auth cold  -> 401
  2 no-auth warm  -> 200 HIT public, max-age=60, s-maxage=31536000, stale-while-revalidate=86400
  3 M156 tok->M18 -> 200 gmv: 968621609500.0
One authorised fetch fills the LRU; the next request with NO Authorization header at all gets 200 with the full KPI payload, and an M156-scoped token reads M18's 968,621,609,500 IRR GMV. cache.middleware is registered at api.py:36 (inner) and short-circuits on hit before FastAPI ever evaluates Depends(_merchant_scope) — exactly the hazard cache.py's own comment says it avoided for /api/admin/* ("the operator gate runs in the route's dependencies, i.e. *after* this middleware"). The comment names the bug and then leaves it open on the merchant routes. Worse, the leaked body ships Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=31536000, so any CDN in front caches one tenant's financials publicly for a year on a URL-only key. `grep -n 'REQUIRE_AUTH|cache.clear|CACHEABLE' tests/` returns no matches: 180 passing tests never exercise this mode or this middleware.
findings.impact: Flipping the documented production switch (ZARIN_REQUIRE_AUTH=1, memory.md "Important env vars") turns authentication into a no-op for every cached merchant endpoint and publishes merchant financials to a shared CDN. The two findings a previous panel rated CRITICAL/HIGH are still exploitable through a different door.
findings.fix: Key the cache on the authenticated principal, or skip the cache entirely when REQUIRE_AUTH is on. Minimal: in cache.middleware, `if REQUIRE_AUTH: return await call_next(request)` before the CACHEABLE check, and set `Cache-Control: private, no-store` for merchant routes in that mode. Add the three-line test from pipeline/_panel/rel_authcache.py.

findings.title: AI-Ops dashboard understates the LLM fallback rate ~10x and LLM p95 latency ~19x, because guard-rejected calls are recorded as source="deterministic"
findings.evidence:
Repro pipeline/_panel/rel_aiops.py — reality: 10 LLM calls (8 guard-rejected @17 000 ms, 2 accepted @900 ms) plus 90 offline deterministic answers.
  dashboard: llm_requests=2 deterministic=98 fallback=8 fallback_rate=0.08 p95=900
True LLM fallback rate 0.80 vs reported 0.08; true LLM p95 ~17 000 ms vs reported 900 ms. Cause: gateway.py:288-296 sets base.fallback=True but leaves base.source=="deterministic" while attaching the real LLM latency/cost, so telemetry.py:55 `llm = [e for e in ev if e.get("source")=="llm"]` drops every failed call from the latency and cost-per-request populations, and telemetry.py:71 divides fallbacks by `total` (which includes 90 requests that could never fall back). The live deployment shows the same signature — GET /api/admin/ai-ops returns fallback=14 with llm_requests=3 (14 > 3 is arithmetically impossible if only LLM calls can fall back), and its latency_ms p95=4873 while GET /api/admin/performance reports /api/copilot/polish p95=15585.2, p99=17339.8 for the same calls. Two panels in the same Control Center disagree 3.5x and the AI one is the optimistic one.
findings.impact: The panel built to prove "the LLM is never on the answer path and we measure when it misbehaves" reports an AI failure rate an order of magnitude below reality and hides the slowest calls entirely. cost_per_request = cost/len(llm) also divides real spend by successes only, overstating unit cost the moment a paid model is used. An operator watching this would never escalate.
findings.fix: Set `base.source = "llm"` in both failure branches (gateway.py:278 and :288) — the call WAS an LLM call, `fallback`/`grounded` already carry the outcome — and change telemetry.py:71 to `fallbacks / len(llm)` with `llm_fallback_rate` as the label.

findings.title: Anonymous callers can evict the request-telemetry ring and inflate the operator response 200x; "attention" is blind to 4xx
findings.location: zarin/obs.py:19 (record uses raw request.url.path), obs.py:22 (_trackable), obs.py:80-88 (attention rules)
findings.evidence:
Repro pipeline/_panel/rel_cardinality.py — 3000 unauthenticated GETs to /api/xxxx<i>:
  ring=3001 endpoint_rows=3001 error_rate=0.0 client_error_rate=0.9997 attention=0 resp_bytes=389184
The path is recorded verbatim and unbounded, so 3000 anonymous 404s produce 3001 rows in /api/admin/performance and a 389 KB response (baseline ~2 KB); at the ring's maxlen=8000 that is ~1 MB re-sorted and shipped on every operator page load, and all real telemetry is evicted. Confirmed live, not just locally: the deployed /api/admin/performance endpoints table contains a row {"path":"/api/nonexistent","count":1,"error_rate":0.0} from one of my probes. Separately, with 99.97% of requests failing 4xx the dashboard reports error_rate 0.0 and attention=[] — obs.py:81-87 only escalates on status>=500 or p95>1500, so an endpoint 4xx-ing on 100% of calls looks perfectly healthy.
findings.impact: An unauthenticated attacker blinds the platform's only request-observability surface and simultaneously degrades it into a multi-hundred-KB payload. A real client-contract break (all 400/422) never raises an attention item, which is precisely the failure mode a payments integration produces.
findings.fix: Bucket unmatched paths: in obs.record, replace the raw path with the matched route template (`request.scope.get("route").path`) and fall back to a single "<unmatched>" label. Add a per-endpoint client_error_rate to obs.summary and one attention rule for it (>0.5 sustained).

findings.title: Server-Timing: app;dur is CDN-cached and excludes cold start — the only latency signal the product exposes is stale and ~50x optimistic
findings.location: zarin/obs.py:41-43 (header set inside the ASGI middleware) + zarin/cache.py:44 (s-maxage=31536000)
findings.evidence:
Stale: `curl -D - 'https://zarbin-nine.vercel.app/api/overview?m=M156&f=2026-01-01&t=2026-06-30&_cb=0'` twice returned `Server-Timing: app;dur=302.9` with `Age: 121` and `X-Vercel-Cache: HIT` — a 121-second-old measurement re-served as this request's server cost, when the true origin cost was zero (the request never reached Python). Three independent 24-way bursts over the same URLs returned byte-identical app p50=106 p95=165 max=303 while wall p50 moved 4298 -> 15776 -> 7476 ms. Scope-blind: pipeline/_panel/cold.py fires 20 concurrent requests with random cache-busters, all X-Vercel-Cache: MISS, so all reach the handler:
  wall p50=3103 p95=4289 max=4452 ms
  app  p50=61   p95=85   max=96 ms
  gap invisible to app;dur: p50=3042 ms max=4356 ms
A single warm sequential /api/meta measured 1916 ms wall against app;dur=18.0. The Control Center's Product Performance panel reports p50 37.8 ms from the same instrument and labels it platform latency.
findings.impact: Both the API's clients and the operator dashboard are told a number that is (a) frozen at cache-fill time on every CDN hit and (b) excludes function boot, queueing and edge time — the dominant components on this deployment. Nobody can see the ~3 s a user actually waits on a cold instance, so the cold-start problem is structurally invisible.
findings.fix: Compute the header from a request-scoped timestamp so a cache hit reports its own (near-zero) cost, and add `Server-Timing: cache;desc=hit` — or simply omit app;dur on the cache-hit branch. Record a process-start timestamp and expose time-since-boot on the first N requests so cold starts show up in obs.summary.

findings.title: Control Center platform health silently resets to near-zero when the serverless instance is recycled, with no indication in the payload
findings.evidence: Within one session against the live deployment, /api/admin/performance reported total=267 (with a populated 19-row endpoint table and p95=3364.5) and, minutes later after a burst, total=7 climbing 7->18 across 12 sequential reads, with the reported p95 flipping 646.7 -> 302.9 mid-sequence purely because the sample was tiny. Nothing in the payload distinguishes "the platform served 7 requests" from "the instance that held the history is gone". The 48 burst requests I made in between never appear at all, because Vercel served them from the edge and the origin never saw them. The durable half is no better on this deploy: memory.md pins ZARIN_TELEMETRY_DIR=/tmp, and locally data/telemetry/ai_events.jsonl has grown from the 48 KB documented in ZB-101 to 205,287 bytes with no rotation, re-read in full by EventLog._warm() on every start.
findings.impact: Every AI-Ops and Product Performance figure is a per-instance, per-lifetime sample of cache misses only, presented without an uptime, sample-window, or instance marker. An operator refreshing the page can see the error rate and p95 change by 2x with zero change in the platform, and post-incident review is impossible because the evidence dies with the lambda.
findings.fix: Return `window_start_ts` / `instance_id` / `uptime_s` alongside every telemetry aggregate and render them, so a reset is visible rather than silent. ADR-0001 already names the durable-store migration; until then, labelling the sample honestly costs three fields.

findings.title: The frontend discards every server error message it is given
findings.evidence: The backend produces specific, actionable errors — verified live: `{"detail":"invalid date for f: 'banana' (expected YYYY-MM-DD)"}`, `{"detail":"merchant NOPE not found"}`, `{"detail":"question too long (max 500 chars)"}`, `{"detail":"unknown outcome: 'DROP'"}`. api.ts throws before reading the body, and ctx.tsx:100/:120 store `String(e)`, which every page renders as `<Empty title="خطا در دریافت داده" body={state.error} />` (Overview.tsx:33, FunnelPage.tsx:21, CustomersPage.tsx:12, PeersPage.tsx:19, ChangesPage.tsx:46, OpsPerformance.tsx:12, OpsAI.tsx:21, OpsSources.tsx:16). The merchant sees the literal string "Error: overview: 400" — untranslated English inside an RTL Persian screen — and is never told which date was wrong. Separately, `grep -n 'AbortController|timeout' frontend/src` returns nothing: no fetch has a timeout or a retry, against measured 3–18 s cold-start waits and a /api/copilot/polish p99 of 17 340 ms.
findings.impact: Careful server-side error engineering is thrown away at the last hop, so no user-facing error is actionable. A hung or cold request spins forever with no timeout and no retry.
findings.fix: In api.ts: `if (!res.ok) { const d = await res.json().catch(() => null); throw new Error(d?.detail ?? `${path}: ${res.status}`); }` and pass an AbortSignal.timeout(20000) to fetch.

findings.title: An inverted date range returns 200 with all-zero money, indistinguishable from "no activity"
findings.location: zarin/api.py:182 _dates — validates each date independently, never the ordering
findings.evidence: GET /api/overview?m=M156&f=2026-06-30&t=2026-01-01 -> HTTP 200, `{"period":{"from":"2026-06-30","to":"2026-01-01"},"kpis":{"gmv":0.0,"verified":0,"sessions":0,"conv":null,...},"daily":[]}`. GET /api/overview?m=M156&f=0001-01-01&t=9999-12-31 -> 200 with the full-dataset totals under a period label spanning ten millennia. On the same empty-window input, /api/customers returns `"summary":{"customers":0}` next to `"interval":{"median_days":27.673125,"n":6707}` and six months of 2026 cohorts, all under `"period":{"from":"2020-01-01","to":"2020-01-02"}`; analytics.py:223 documents the full-window choice for the UI, but nothing in the JSON marks those two blocks as out-of-period, and /api/openapi.json does not either. /api/peers on the same window reports me.sessions=55940 with `evidence.period: "2020-01-01 تا 2020-01-02"`.
findings.impact: A client date-picker bug or a transposed parameter yields a confident "you earned zero" instead of an error, and machine consumers of the public API (advertised at /api/docs) get full-history figures stamped with a period they do not belong to.
findings.fix: One guard in _dates: `if f > t: raise HTTPException(400, f"f ({f}) is after t ({t})")` — all seven merchant routes go through it. Add a `scope: "full_history"` marker to the customers `interval`/`cohorts` blocks and to the peers `me` block.

findings.title: 500s return text/plain with no error envelope and no correlation id recorded anywhere
findings.evidence: Forcing an exception in analytics.overview: `status: 500 ctype: text/plain; charset=utf-8 cache-control: None body: Internal Server Error`. Every other error on the API is `application/json {"detail": ...}`, so a client doing res.json() on failure gets a SyntaxError instead of a status. The platform does emit `X-Vercel-Id: fra1::fra1::m4rtf-1787384297687-0e7703e56255`, but obs.record (obs.py:19) stores only method/path/status/latency/t, so an operator who sees the error spike in the Control Center has no id to join against the Vercel log line. Also verified in the same run: the ZB-021 fix genuinely works — obs recorded error_rate 1.0 and raised `{'severity':'high','path':'/api/overview','fa':'مسیر /api/overview نرخ خطای سرور ۱۰۰٪ دارد'}`.
findings.impact: Inconsistent error contract on the one path where the client most needs to parse a response, and no way to correlate a reported failure with a log line.
findings.fix: Add `@app.exception_handler(Exception)` returning `JSONResponse({"detail": "internal error", "request_id": rid}, 500)`, and put `rid` (from X-Vercel-Id or a uuid4) into the obs event and an X-Request-Id response header.

lenses.summary: Server-side latency on the live deployment is real and honest: cold origin costs are 17.7 ms (/api/meta) to 191.8 ms (/api/customers), warm merchant endpoints sit at 25-50 ms, and I confirmed Server-Timing is not hiding queue time by running the control — 24 concurrent origin requests gave TTFB 1.8-3.8 s with app;dur 24.7-239.3 ms, but 24 concurrent requests for a static CDN asset that never touches the function gave the same 1.8-4.9 s spread, so the gap is my network to fra1, not the app. The design underneath is also sound where it matters: parquet_metadata() shows only 1 of 17 row groups (122,880 of 2,062,839 rows = 6.0%) is touched for a merchant filter, the per-thread-cursor DuckDB pattern took 192 concurrent requests with 0 errors, and peak working set is 154 MB over 63 MB of marts. What it does not survive is load or growth. Throughput peaks at 19.6 req/s at concurrency 4 and *falls* to 13.4 req/s at 32 while p99 goes 381 ms → 7,113 ms; on a 10x mart I built (20.6M sessions) peak throughput is 8.0 req/s, p99 19,836 ms, and peak RSS is 1,720 MB while DuckDB believes it has a 25 GiB memory_limit and points temp_directory at a relative '.tmp' that is read-only on Vercel. And the response cache returns bodies before FastAPI resolves Depends(_merchant_scope): with ZARIN_REQUIRE_AUTH=1, one authenticated fetch of M156 makes the identical 22,378-byte payload available to an anonymous caller and to a token scoped to a different merchant.
lenses.not_higher_because: Three measured behaviours would block a real fintech deployment. (1) The system scales negatively: adding concurrency past 4 reduces throughput and multiplies p99 by 18.7x, because PRAGMA threads=4 on one shared DuckDB instance is fed by a 44-thread anyio pool with no admission control. (2) There is no memory back-pressure and no working spill path — DuckDB's memory_limit is left at its 25 GiB default and temp_directory at a relative path that is read-only on the target platform, so the 1,720 MB peak I measured at 10x becomes a silent OOM kill rather than a slow query. (3) The response cache short-circuits the merchant auth dependency, which I demonstrated end to end; the cache module's own docstring reasons about exactly this hazard for /api/admin/* and then misses it for the merchant routes. Add the architectural ceiling — 63 MB of parquet ships inside the function bundle, so 10x is a deploy failure, not a latency regression — and the ops telemetry that samples one lambda's ring buffer, and this is not "minor gaps".
lenses.not_lower_because: Every performance claim I tried to break held up under an adversarial control. I assumed Server-Timing was under-reporting queue time and built the static-asset control to prove it; it did not — app;dur is an honest server-side number and the live warm p50 really is ~35 ms. I assumed the sorted-parquet claim in memory.md was decoration; parquet_metadata() shows 6.0% of rows scanned per merchant query, so it is buying real I/O reduction. I assumed the shared DuckDB connection would corrupt or error under load; the thread-local .cursor() pattern is the documented-safe one and survived 192 concurrent requests with 0 errors. I assumed the CDN's year-long s-maxage was pinning something mutable; I dumped every cacheable body looking for a generated_at, a counter, or a telemetry-derived field and found none. And the caching is a genuine fix rather than a slow query in a costume — the underlying uncached costs are 17-192 ms, so full coverage of 343 merchants across 9 endpoints is about five minutes of one-off CPU. Nothing here is fabricated or hand-waved, which is what separates this from the 40-59 band.
verified_strengths: Server-Timing is honest, and I tried to prove otherwise. Suspecting app;dur excluded queue time, I ran 24 concurrent origin requests (TTFB 1.802-3.781 s, app;dur 24.7-239.3 ms) and then the control — 24 concurrent requests for a static CDN asset that never touches the function — which produced the same 1.843-4.859 s spread. The gap is my own network to fra1, not hidden server time. Sequential warm merchant endpoints on the live deploy are genuinely 25-50 ms server-side.

The sorted-parquet claim in memory.md pays off in real I/O. `SELECT row_group_id, stats_min, stats_max FROM parquet_metadata('data/marts/sessions.parquet') WHERE path_in_schema='merchant_key'` returns 17 row groups over 2,062,839 rows, of which exactly 1 (122,880 rows = 6.0%) has a [min,max] spanning M156; attempts.parquet is 1 of 16 (6.3%). Merchant queries touch ~6% of the file, not all of it.

The DuckDB concurrency pattern is the correct one, not a lucky accident. zarin/db.py:38-51 gives each thread its own .cursor() off a single shared connection via threading.local, which is the documented-safe DuckDB idiom (sharing the connection object's execute() across threads is not). I drove 192 concurrent requests and 900+ total through it with 0 errors and no wrong results.

Memory at the shipped scale is genuinely small because the marts stay as parquet views with projection/predicate pushdown rather than being materialised: PeakWorkingSet64 of the whole uvicorn process was 154 MB after a 32-concurrent load over 63 MB of marts, and a single /api/customers peaks at 89 MB in a fresh process. DuckDB's connect()+CREATE VIEW+schema guard costs 21 ms and count(*) over the full mart is 2 ms (parquet metadata, not a scan).

Every CDN-cacheable body really is a pure function of path+query, which is what the year-long s-maxage depends on. I dumped /api/meta (keys: range, merchants, demo, notes) and /api/quality (outcomes, concentration, anomalies, rules_fa) specifically hunting for a generated_at, a request counter, or a telemetry-derived field that a 31536000 s edge TTL would freeze into a lie. There is none — the demo presets are computed from merchant_stats and the anomaly counts come from the pipeline sidecar.

findings.title: Response cache returns merchant data before the merchant auth dependency runs
findings.evidence: With ZARIN_REQUIRE_AUTH=1 and a cold cache, an unauthenticated GET /api/overview?m=M156 correctly returns 401. After ONE authenticated request warms the cache, the same anonymous request returns 200 with X-Zarbin-Cache: HIT and a byte-identical body (verified: `bodies identical: True`, 22,378 bytes), and a bearer token scoped to merchant M18 also gets M156's payload with 200 / HIT. Full run: `authed: 200 MISS public, max-age=60, s-maxage=31536000, stale-while-revalidate=86400` / `no-auth: 200 HIT 22378` / `bodies identical: True` / `wrong-merchant: 200 HIT` / `cold no-auth: 401`. The middleware returns from its `_get(key)` branch before `call_next`, so Depends(_merchant_scope) never executes. The same response carries `Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=31536000`, so a shared CDN would also store one merchant's financial data for a year under a key any caller can construct.
findings.impact: In the product's own documented production posture (ZARIN_REQUIRE_AUTH=1, which is what the prod-shaped migration path calls for), the merchant isolation control is a no-op for every cached path. Not currently exploitable on zarbin-nine.vercel.app because REQUIRE_AUTH defaults to off (zarin/config.py:26) and the merchant API is deliberately public there — but the flag is the supported way to turn isolation on, and turning it on does not turn it on. cache.py's docstring excludes /api/admin/* for precisely this reason ("the operator gate runs in the route's dependencies, i.e. *after* this middleware") and then misses the identical hazard one route group over.
findings.fix: In cache.middleware, skip the cache entirely when REQUIRE_AUTH is set or an Authorization header is present, or fold the verified principal into the cache key: `key = f"{path}?{request.url.query}|{principal}"`. Two lines, and it also stops `public` from being emitted for per-merchant bodies.

findings.title: Throughput decreases under concurrency; p99 rises 18.7x from 4 to 32 in-flight requests
findings.location: zarin/db.py:35 (PRAGMA threads=4 on one shared connection) + all sync routes in zarin/api.py
findings.evidence: Load driver against the real uvicorn server, distinct cache-busting keys so every request reaches DuckDB, 8 logical cores. 1x marts: conc=1 7.5 req/s p99=381ms; conc=4 19.6 req/s p99=462ms; conc=8 18.7 req/s p99=1547ms; conc=16 16.3 req/s p99=2683ms; conc=32 13.4 req/s p99=7113ms (0 errors). Peak throughput is at concurrency 4 and every step beyond it is slower in both throughput and tail. On 10x marts: conc=4 5.8 req/s; conc=8 8.0 req/s (peak); conc=32 6.4 req/s p99=19836ms max=24455ms. The server process carried 44 OS threads while only 4 DuckDB workers exist.
findings.impact: The system has a hard ceiling near 20 req/s and gets worse, not better, when pushed. On Vercel with in-instance concurrency this is the live behaviour of a single warm lambda; the 24.5 s worst case at 10x is inside maxDuration:60 today but not with any headroom. There is no admission control, so an overload degrades everyone's tail instead of shedding.
findings.fix: Put a `threading.Semaphore(N)` around db.q/q1 sized to the DuckDB thread budget so surplus requests queue cheaply instead of thrashing the 4 workers and the GIL, and set PRAGMA threads from the container's actual vCPU count rather than the hardcoded 4.

findings.title: No DuckDB memory limit and a spill directory on a read-only filesystem; peak RSS is 11x at 10x data
findings.evidence: `current_setting('memory_limit')` = 25.0 GiB (DuckDB's 80%-of-host default) and `current_setting('temp_directory')` = `.tmp`, a relative path. grep across zarin/ for memory_limit|temp_directory|max_memory returns only the threads pragma. Measured PeakWorkingSet64 after the same 32-concurrent load: 154 MB on the 1x server, 1,720 MB on the 10x server (steady state 146 MB and 174 MB respectively). A single /api/customers?m=M156 in a fresh process: peak 89 MB at 1x, 264 MB at 10x. memory.md states the deployment target is read-only except ZARIN_TELEMETRY_DIR=/tmp/...
findings.impact: DuckDB sizes its buffer pool from the host's RAM, not the function's allowance, so it never applies back-pressure inside a 1024-1769 MB serverless container; and the one escape valve — spilling — writes to a relative path that is read-only in production. The failure mode at scale is a hard OOM kill with no diagnostic, not a slow query. The 1,720 MB I measured at 10x already exceeds a 1 GB function.
findings.fix: Two lines in connect(): `PRAGMA memory_limit='768MB'` (or the function memory minus headroom, from an env var) and `PRAGMA temp_directory='/tmp/duckdb'`.

findings.title: Control Center performance telemetry is a per-instance in-memory ring and is blind to every CDN hit
findings.evidence: Immediately after issuing 60+ API calls to the live deployment (8 endpoints cold, 6 sequential origin hits, 24 concurrent fan-out, 3 copilot calls), GET /api/admin/performance returned `{"total":40,"throughput_rps":0.16,"latency_ms":{"p50":35.4,"p95":222.4,"p99":512.9}}` and an endpoints list containing only /api/overview (24), /api/copilot (3), /api/admin/copilot (3), /api/admin/sources (3), /api/admin/ai-ops (6), /api/admin/merchants (1). There is no row at all for /api/meta, /api/insights, /api/funnel, /api/customers, /api/peers, /api/quality or /api/evidence/sessions, every one of which I called against that host.
findings.impact: The surface that answers "how is Zarbin itself doing?" reports one lambda's slice. Two independent losses: requests spread across instances that each keep their own ring (and lose it on recycle, durable=False), and CDN HITs never reach the origin at all — so the better the cache performs, the more the ops dashboard under-counts. throughput_rps, error_rate and the p50/p95/p99 shown to an operator are not platform figures and are not labelled as samples.
findings.fix: Either label the panel as per-instance in the UI and the API payload (cheap, honest), or push request events to a shared store; and count CDN-served traffic separately so the dashboard does not silently equate 'origin requests' with 'traffic'.

findings.title: Two of the five /api/customers queries ignore the selected date window, so narrowing the period cannot reduce the cost
findings.evidence: Both filter only `WHERE merchant_key=$m AND outcome='verified'` with no `d BETWEEN $f AND $t`, while the sibling queries use PERIOD_SQL. `interval` runs `lag(created_at) OVER (PARTITION BY payer_card_key ORDER BY created_at)` and `cohorts` runs a datediff group-by with count(DISTINCT card) — both full sorts over the merchant's entire history. Measured at 10x, Server-Timing app;dur: 6-month window 1905.1 / 1541.5 ms vs a 1-week window (26x smaller) 755.3 / 599.5 ms — only 2.5x cheaper. The control, /api/overview at 10x, goes 168.1 → 101.4 ms on the same two windows. /api/customers is also the worst scaler in the suite: 1x 170/161/204 ms → 10x 1244/1322/1165 ms (7.0x, near-linear), against 2.4x for overview, 2.9x for insights and 1.2x for peers.
findings.impact: A ~600 ms per-request floor at 10x that no user action can reduce, and the endpoint that degrades closest to linearly with dataset size. At 100x it is ~6 s of unavoidable work per uncached call.
findings.fix: Add the period predicate to the interval and cohort CTEs (they already receive f/t in `p`), or compute lifetime cohort/interval figures once in the pipeline into a mart instead of per request.

findings.title: Unknown query params are part of the cache key but not of the response — unauthenticated cache dilution with no rate limit
findings.location: zarin/cache.py:99 (key = f"{path}?{request.url.query}") and the Vercel edge key
findings.evidence: Live: /api/overview?m=M156&junk=<random> returns the same 22,378-byte body as the canonical URL. First request X-Vercel-Cache: MISS with Server-Timing app;dur=36.1/42.2/37.2 ms at the origin; repeating the *same* junk key returns X-Vercel-Cache: HIT — so each junk key becomes its own edge object pinned by s-maxage=31536000. Locally I evicted the process cache with junk alone: first key MISS → HIT → MISS after 600 distinct junk keys. grep across zarin/ for ratelimit|rate_limit|slowapi|throttle: no hits.
findings.impact: Any anonymous client can force unlimited origin computation (~40 ms of DuckDB each, and 190 ms if it picks /api/customers), evict the entire in-process cache with 512 cheap requests, and fill the edge with year-lived garbage objects. No authentication, no rate limit, no cost to the attacker.
findings.fix: Build the key from the parameters the route actually declares (FastAPI already knows them via request.scope['route'].dependant.query_params) rather than the raw query string.

findings.title: In-process LRU is sized below its own working set and has a ~2% hit rate behind the CDN
findings.evidence: After walking 60 merchants x 5 endpoints: `{'entries': 303, 'hits': 6, 'misses': 303, 'hit_rate': 0.0194}`. 343 merchants x 5 core endpoints = 1,715 keys for the default window alone, before any date range, so at most 30% of the minimum working set fits; 600 distinct keys evicted the first entry, confirmed by MISS on re-read. On the live deployment every single response I observed across ~40 distinct requests carried X-Zarbin-Cache: MISS, because the CDN absorbs all the repeats and only never-seen keys reach the process. Worst-case resident bound is also expressed in entries, not bytes: 512 x MAX_BODY_BYTES(2,000,000) = 1.02 GB (not reachable today — the largest body is /api/meta at 51,778 B, so realistically ~26 MB).
findings.impact: The second cache layer buys ~2% of requests behind a CDN while carrying the auth-bypass risk of finding 1. Its stated purpose (a cold edge, or a deployment with no CDN) is real but it is sized for neither.
findings.fix: Either raise MAX_ENTRIES above the merchant x endpoint product and bound the store by total bytes instead of entry count, or delete the layer and rely on the CDN — the measured hit rate does not currently justify it.

findings.title: Control Center's full-platform scans can never be edge-cached, so every cold instance repays them
findings.evidence: Live, first call on a fresh instance: /api/admin/platform Server-Timing app;dur=504.8 ms, /api/admin/ai-eval app;dur=935.2 ms, /api/admin/sources 79.1 ms, /api/admin/merchants 68.4 ms; second call 5.0 / 2.1 / 22.7 / 1.9 ms. All carry Cache-Control: no-store (correctly — the ops guard runs after the cache middleware). On 10x marts locally the cold numbers become 1,436.5 ms and 3,409.3 ms. control.py's own comment states each platform call "costs a full-platform scan of 2.06M sessions".
findings.impact: The memoisation is per-process, so it helps a single warm lambda and nothing else: every scale-out, every recycle, and every concurrent request that lands on a new instance pays the full scan. Extrapolating the measured 1x→10x factor, at 100x platform is ~14 s and ai-eval ~34 s against maxDuration: 60.
findings.fix: Precompute the platform aggregate per (window) into a small mart at build time — the marts are immutable for the life of the deployment, so there is nothing to compute at request time — and move the retrieval eval out of the request path into a build artifact the endpoint reads.

findings.title: Marts ship inside the function bundle, and .vercelignore denies paths under data/ by name rather than allowing only data/marts
findings.evidence: Measured bundle contents: data/marts 63 MB + zarin 1.8 MB (incl. 1.1 MB built SPA) + public 1.1 MB, plus the requirements wheels (duckdb 0.66 MB, fastapi 1.6 MB, pydantic 3.6 MB, pydantic_core 5.4 MB, starlette 0.66 MB) ≈ 78 MB unzipped. .vercelignore excludes `data/telemetry` and `data/other_challenge_data.csv.gz` by explicit name and has no rule covering anything else under data/. I created data/_marts10x (147 MB) during this review and nothing in the ignore list would have kept it out of a deploy (removed afterwards).
findings.impact: 10x the dataset is 630 MB of marts and 100x is 6.3 GB, past Vercel's 250 MB unzipped function limit — so the 10x break point is a deploy failure, not a latency regression, and the migration off this packaging model is a rewrite of the storage layer rather than a config change. Separately, the denylist shape means any future directory under data/ silently doubles the bundle.
findings.fix: Invert the data/ rule to an allowlist (`data/*` then `!data/marts`), and record the bundle-size ceiling in docs/DEPLOY_VERCEL.md next to the .vercelignore invariant so the growth limit is a known constraint rather than a surprise.

findings.title: Three declared font weights are never referenced by any rule
findings.evidence: The built CSS declares @font-face for weights 100,200,300,400,500,600,700,800,900. Scanning the non-@font-face CSS plus the JS bundle for font-weight / fontWeight values yields only 400,500,600,700,800,900. Vazirmatn-Thin (50,796 B), ExtraLight (51,268 B) and Light (51,180 B) — 153 KB of woff2 — ship in the deployment and no rule can ever trigger their download.
findings.impact: Dead weight in the deploy artifact only; browsers will not fetch an unreferenced face, so there is no runtime cost to a visitor. Noted because everything else on the front end is measurably clean: brotli at the edge takes the 628 KB JS to 181,594 B and the 51,778 B /api/meta to 5,918 B, and font-display:swap is set on every face.
findings.fix: Drop the three unused weights from the font import in the frontend source; -153 KB from the bundle for a one-line change.

lenses.summary: I ran the insight engine over all 343 merchants on two windows and probed the live deployment. Coverage is genuinely well-calibrated: 95.0% of platform GMV and 98.6% of sessions belong to a merchant that gets at least one money-denominated opportunity card, and among merchants with >=100 in-window sessions only 2.7% (2/73) get an empty feed on the 30-day view. The 22% of merchants who get nothing over 6 months have a median of 5 sessions — that is restraint, not emptiness. Peer benchmarking works for 343/343 merchants (median 13 peers), and card anatomy is real: the gmv_change card attributes the delta to traffic vs basket vs conversion and swaps the action accordingly, and each card routes to its supporting page. The last mile is thinner than it looks: only 4 of N cards ever render (8 opportunity cards across 15 merchants are unreachable, including two paid_unverified cards that are real collectable money), "فعلاً نه" is a dead control, and the "what to do" text is one of only 19 fixed strings across 538 cards — the action never carries the hour, amount-band or error-code detail the product already computes. The two surfaces are genuinely different products (API percentiles, AI grounding/cost, source adapters, a sortable follow-up table — none of it on the merchant side), but the Control Center's own assistant is 8 regexes with a catch-all, and its AI-Ops headline numbers dropped from total=128/hallucination_risk=23 to total=6/hallucination_risk=0 across two calls four minutes apart on the same token.
lenses.not_higher_because: The product's own claim 7 ("answers the question that was asked, or refuses and says why") is falsified on both surfaces with reproducible evidence, at confidence=high rather than a clarify. The ops copilot has no refusal path in its code at all — every unmatched question returns the platform status line. On the merchant side the flagship merchant M31 (312,814 sessions, the largest in the dataset) is shown a top opportunity of exactly 114,479,770,001 IRR — 100.0% of its entire realized GMV — as a point estimate (low=mid=high), and demo merchant M265 shows the same shape. The GMV clamp fires on 22 cards with a median pre-clamp overshoot of 4.3x and a max of 100x, so the clamp is masking an estimator that is wrong by orders of magnitude, not trimming an edge. And the operator's single data-staleness signal reads 2018-10-20 for a 2026 dataset, badged green. A serious team would not ship the ops copilot or the M31 card in this state.
lenses.not_lower_because: Coverage is measured, targeted and defensible rather than a demo-merchant illusion: I generated cards for every one of the 343 merchants, not just the 5 in meta.demo, and 143 merchants carrying 95% of GMV get a rial-denominated opportunity. Every card I read end-to-end contained the merchant's own numbers, a named counterparty where one exists (PSP-03 at 20.8% first-attempt success vs PSP-04 at 60.8% on the same merchant's traffic, with the top error codes), an effort chip, a sample size, and an evidence drawer. The empty state is two-branch and honest — a weak funnel gets "your conversion is X, that is not good news" plus a button to the funnel page, a healthy one gets "no gap found, that is a good sign". The click-through map (CARD_TARGET) and the done/skip checklist are real last-mile work, not decoration. And the Control Center is not a re-skin: it carries latency percentiles, AI fallback/grounding/cost, adapter status and a merchant follow-up table sortable by unverified money, all absent from the merchant surface.
verified_strengths: Coverage is calibrated, not lazy, and I measured it end to end rather than trusting the claim: generating cards for all 343 merchants (not the 5 in meta.demo) gives 95.0% of platform GMV and 98.6% of sessions belonging to a merchant with at least one rial-denominated opportunity card, from only 143/343 merchants. The 75 merchants who get nothing over 6 months have a median of 5 sessions and 4.32% of GMV between them.

Restraint holds on the window that matters most. Re-running the engine on the last 30 days and gating on in-window volume: of 73 merchants with >=100 sessions in the window only 2 (2.7%) get an empty feed, and of the 40 with >=500 sessions, zero do. The naive "50% of merchants see nothing on 30 days" reading is an artifact of 178 merchants with almost no traffic.

Peer benchmarking — the stated differentiator — actually works for the whole population, not just showcase merchants. Calling peers.peer_group for every merchant: 343/343 return sufficient=True, peer count min 5, p25 12, median 13, max 33. The 38 merchants with fewer than 8 peers get an explicit "مقایسه با N همتا — نامطمئن" chip in InsightCard.tsx, which I confirmed fires on M156 (n_peers=5) in the live /api/insights payload.

The change card is genuinely diagnostic, not a delta restatement. Reading the 538 generated cards, gmv_change attributes the move to traffic vs basket size vs conversion and swaps the action accordingly — M43 got "افت ۷۲٪ … کاهش ترافیک عامل اصلی بوده — کانال‌های جذب را بررسی کنید" while M18 got "رشد ۲۵٪ … رشد از بزرگ‌تر شدن سبد خرید آمده — همین ترکیب محصول/قیمت را حفظ کنید". The live copilot reproduces the same decomposition with signed contributions per factor.

The two surfaces are genuinely different products, verified by pulling all five admin payloads with an ops token: /api/admin/performance carries per-endpoint p50/p95/p99 and an attention list, /api/admin/ai-ops carries grounded_rate, fallback_rate, token and cost totals and per-intent counts, /api/admin/sources carries adapter status with a truth-source flag, /api/admin/platform carries category distribution and top5_share concentration. None of these fields appears on any merchant endpoint, and the merchant surface's peer/funnel/customer analytics appear on none of the admin ones.

findings.title: Ops copilot has no refusal path — every unmatched question returns the platform status line at confidence=high
findings.evidence:
Live, with an ops session token, three unrelated questions to /api/admin/copilot returned identical intent=system, confidence=high:
  Q "وضعیت پلتفرم چطور است؟" -> "وضعیت کلی: ۳۴۳ پذیرندهٔ فعال…"
  Q "کدام پذیرنده بیشترین پول تاییدنشده دارد؟" -> "وضعیت کلی: ۳۴۳ پذیرندهٔ فعال…" (names no merchant)
  Q "چه کاری باید انجام بدم؟" -> "وضعیت کلی: ۳۴۳ پذیرندهٔ فعال…"
Reading zarin/ops_copilot.py: _plan() is 8 regexes and then an unconditional `return _system(f, t)`. There is no clarify/unrecognised branch and no retrieval layer — the merchant side got nlu.py (522 lines, calibrated by pipeline/calibrate_nlu.py, evaluated by zarin.ai.eval.retrieval); the ops side got none of it, while its docstring claims "Same two-stage contract as the merchant copilot".
findings.impact: Product claim 7 is false for the entire Control Center. The specific question asked ("which merchant has the most unverified money?") is answerable from /api/admin/merchants?sort=unverified, which the same surface already serves — so an operator is confidently given an unrelated summary instead of the answer sitting one endpoint away.
findings.fix: Add an unrecognised branch before the catch-all: if no regex matched, return confidence="low" with the list of ops intents it can answer (mirroring copilot.py's clarify plan). Route the merchant-naming questions to control.merchants() with the existing sort keys.

findings.title: Merchant copilot answers "how much money did I lose?" with total successful sales, at confidence=high
findings.location: zarin/nlu.py:375 (gmv intent anchor "چقدر پول", weighted x4)
findings.evidence: Offline and live agree. `copilot.route_detail('چقدر پول از دست دادم؟')` returns `('gmv', 'search')`; `copilot.answer('M156', 'چقدر پول از دست دادم؟', ...)` returns intent=gmv, confidence=high, answer "در این بازه ۵۵٬۹۴۰ جلسهٔ پرداخت ثبت شد و ۳۰٬۵۰۸ پرداخت به تایید رسید؛ فروش موفق ۱٫۹۵ هزار میلیارد ریال…". Live /api/copilot?m=M156 gives the identical answer. Three near-synonyms behave correctly (چقدر فروش از دست دادم؟ / ضرر من چقدر بوده؟ / چقدر درآمد از دست رفته دارم؟ all -> intent=clarify, confidence=low with suggestions), so this is one anchor, not a systemic router failure: the literal string "چقدر پول" is a gmv anchor and matches the question verbatim.
findings.impact: The single most commercially loaded question a merchant can ask is answered with the opposite number — revenue earned reported as if it were revenue lost — with no clarification and a high-confidence badge. The product can answer it (the priorities/opportunity engine computes exactly this) but never gets the chance.
findings.fix: Narrow the gmv anchor from "چقدر پول" to "چقدر پول گرفتم"/"چقدر پول رسید", and add "چقدر پول از دست دادم" to the priorities intent examples in nlu.py. Re-run `python -m zarin.ai.eval.retrieval -v` to confirm no regression.

findings.title: Largest merchant's headline opportunity is 100.0% of its entire GMV, rendered as a point estimate with no interval
findings.location: zarin/insights.py:605-650 (_apply_gmv_cap) — observed live on M31 and demo merchant M265
findings.evidence: Live GET /api/insights?m=M31 returns card 1 = inbank_gap, impact_low = impact_mid = impact_high = 114479770001, capped=true. That is exactly M31's realized 6-month GMV (114,479.8M IRR) for a merchant with 312,814 sessions. Demo merchant M265 (in meta.demo, so a first-click path) shows the same shape: no_attempt_gap, lo=mid=hi=4355020000, capped=true. Instrumenting _apply_gmv_cap over all 343 merchants: 22 cards had a pre-clamp estimate exceeding total GMV, ratio est/GMV min 1.06, median 4.27, max 100.21. Because low==high, frontend/src/components/InsightCard.tsx computes hasInterval=false and prints a single number — the least credible estimate gets the most confident presentation.
findings.impact: A merchant is told it can recover an amount equal to every rial it earned in six months, stated as one exact figure. That is not a decision, and it undermines claim 5 ("opportunity is a counterfactual peer-gap estimate, capped at realized GMV") by showing that the cap is load-bearing rather than a guard rail. It lands on the biggest merchant in the dataset and on a curated demo merchant.
findings.fix: When the clamp binds, stop publishing a rial figure at all: convert the card to an alert the way the realized<=0 branch already does (insights.py:631-641), keeping the rate comparison ("your 71.8% vs peer median 28.6%") which is the real finding, and drop the money. At minimum never collapse low/mid/high to one value — a clamped estimate should widen, not narrow.

findings.title: Control Center AI-Ops health numbers are per-lambda and change by 20x between refreshes
findings.evidence:
Same ops token, same endpoint, ~4 minutes apart against https://zarbin-nine.vercel.app/api/admin/ai-ops:
  call A: total=128, llm_requests=13, grounded_rate=0.8203, fallback_rate=0.1797, hallucination_risk=23, zero_evidence=58
  calls B-G (6 consecutive): total=6, llm_requests=0, grounded_rate=1.0, fallback_rate=0.0, hallucination_risk=0
No data was deleted between the calls; the count went down. memory.md itself records ZARIN_TELEMETRY_DIR=/tmp as a deployment invariant, so each warm serverless instance keeps its own ring.
findings.impact: The AI Operations page is the reason the Control Center exists as a separate product, and its headline quality metric is non-reproducible. An operator who sees hallucination_risk=23 and refreshes to 0 cannot act on either number, and the 100%-grounded reading is survivorship bias from a cold instance.
findings.fix: Either persist the telemetry ring outside per-instance /tmp, or label the page honestly — show the instance id and "since this instance warmed at <ts>" next to the totals so the operator knows the denominator is a sample, not the platform.

findings.title: Data-source freshness is the parquet file's mtime, reading 2018-10-20 for a 2026 dataset, badged "connected/ok"
findings.evidence: Live GET /api/admin/sources, three consecutive calls, all return: zarinpal, status=ok, is_truth=true, freshness="2018-10-20T01:46:40+00:00". The dataset range from /api/meta is 2026-01-01 to 2026-06-30. frontend/src/ops/OpsSources.tsx renders it verbatim as "تازگی داده: <localized 2018 date>" next to a green متصل chip. The value is exactly epoch 1540000000 — a build-artifact mtime, not a data timestamp.
findings.impact: Freshness is the one signal an operator uses to decide whether the pipeline is stale, and on the deployed product it is wrong by eight years while the source is badged healthy. It also contradicts the page's own premise ("the challenge dataset is one input, not the whole system") — a real second source would need a real freshness contract.
findings.fix: Report `max(d)` from the sessions mart (the data's own recency) instead of the file mtime, and let the adapter carry both: `data_through` (from the mart) shown to the operator, `built_at` (mtime) as a build detail.

findings.title: Overview renders only 4 cards with no "show more" — 8 opportunity cards are unreachable, including two of real collectable money
findings.evidence: Ran insights.generate over all 343 merchants: 15 merchants produce more than 4 cards (5:11, 6:2, 7:2). The cards beyond index 3 are: gmv_change x13, repeat_gap x4, paid_unverified x2, recovery_gap x1, psp_friction x1 — 8 of them card_type="opportunity", largest hidden impact 742,632,468 IRR. Confirmed the API is not the limiter: live GET /api/insights?m=M250 returns 5 cards, the UI shows 4. There is no other consumer of the insights payload in the frontend (grep: only Overview.tsx renders cards), so there is no second place to see them.
findings.impact: Two merchants have a paid_unverified card — settled bank money the merchant can collect today, the product's strongest and most concrete play — silently truncated off the page with no affordance suggesting anything is missing.
findings.fix: Render all cards, or keep the 4-card fold and add a "نمایش N مورد دیگر" toggle. paid_unverified should never be foldable: it is realized money, not an estimate.

findings.title: The action text is one of 19 fixed strings across 538 cards and never uses the merchant-specific diagnosis the product already computes
findings.evidence: Collected action_fa for every card generated across all 343 merchants: 538 cards, 19 distinct strings. Only 4 of the 19 vary by merchant, and only by substituting a PSP code ("…سهم ترافیک را از PSP-03 به درگاه قوی‌تر منتقل کند"). The three most common — 77x "لاگ خطای فراخوانی verify را بررسی کنید", 69x "با پشتیبانی زرین‌پال درباره درگاه/PSP جایگزین صحبت کنید", 62x "مسیر انتقال به درگاه را روی موبایل و دسکتاپ تست کنید" — are identical for every merchant that receives them. Meanwhile the same engine already computes per-merchant hour-of-day conversion (copilot intent `hours` returned "ضعیف‌ترین نرخ تبدیل در ساعت ۳ است" for M156), amount-band conversion, and top switch error codes — none of which reaches the action line.
findings.impact: Observation and diagnosis are merchant-specific and quantified; the action — the part that is supposed to make this a decision rather than a dashboard — is a static playbook. "Test your redirect on mobile and desktop" is the same sentence whether the no-attempt rate is 14.7% (M43) or 94.4% (M265), two completely different failure modes.
findings.fix: Parameterise the top 3 action strings with the detail already in _Ctx: name the worst hour/amount band in the friction actions, and name the top error code in the inbank action. One f-string per generator, no new queries.

findings.title: Control Center identifies which merchants to act on but the rows are dead text — no route into that merchant's workspace
findings.evidence: The platform insight's action reads "پذیرندگان دارای بیشترین مبلغ تاییدنشده را برای فعال‌سازی وریفای خودکار پیگیری کنید" (zarin/control.py:146) and the table below it is sortable by unverified money (SORTS includes `unverified`), so the operator can find the target — live /api/admin/merchants returns e.g. M156 with paid_unverified_amount=61,847,264,950 over 912 payments. But merchant_key renders as plain text: no link, no onClick, no setMerchant. The app already has `setMerchant` in ctx and a workspace switcher in App.tsx, so the destination exists.
findings.impact: The ops workflow terminates at a row. An operator who has just been told to chase the top unverified merchants has to memorise a key, switch workspace, and hunt it out of a 343-entry select — for the single most common ops action the product recommends.
findings.fix: Make the cell a button that calls `setMerchant(r.merchant_key)` and switches to the merchant workspace overview. One onClick.

findings.title: One in five merchants gets exactly one card and it is a score-0 "sales changed" alert
findings.evidence: Across all 343 merchants on the default 6-month window: 67 merchants (19.5%) produce exactly one card and it is `gmv_change`. gmv_change is the most-generated card overall (167 of 538) and _score() assigns card_type != "opportunity" a score of 0 by construction. 200 of 343 merchants (58.3%) get zero opportunity cards at all; within the >=100-session cohort that is still 20 of 156 (12.8%).
findings.impact: For a fifth of the merchant base the entire "مهم‌ترین فرصت‌های شما" section is a restatement of a number already on the KPI strip above it ("sales grew 25%"), presented in the priority-card frame. That is the dashboard failure mode the product is explicitly positioned against, and it is worse than the honest empty state those merchants would otherwise get.
findings.fix: Do not let gmv_change be the only card. If it is the sole survivor, either fall back to _card_absolute_funnel (already written, currently only reachable when the card list is completely empty) or render it below the section in a plain "what changed" strip rather than as priority #1.

findings.title: "فعلاً نه" (skip) is a dead control — it changes nothing about the card or the feed
findings.evidence: `saveStatus` persists both "done" and "skip" to localStorage, but only "done" is consumed: line 64 sets `opacity: status === "done" ? 0.6 : 1`, and the انجام شد chip renders on `status === "done"`. Nothing anywhere reads "skip" except the button's own aria-pressed. There is no filtering or re-sorting on status for either value, so even a card marked done keeps its rank and still consumes one of the four visible slots.
findings.impact: The checklist offers two verbs and honours one and a half. A merchant who dismisses a card sees it return, unchanged, at the same rank, on the next visit — the affordance teaches them the checklist does not work.
findings.fix: Sort dismissed cards (done or skip) to the end of the list before the slice(0,4), and give skip the same muted treatment as done. Both are two lines in Overview.tsx/InsightCard.tsx; no backend change.

lenses.summary: I recomputed the headline value number straight from the parquet and it is exact: platform paid_unverified = 8,706 sessions / 116,550,558,678 IRR, byte-identical to /api/admin/platform. That is 2.26% of the 5,165bn IRR verified GMV — real, traceable, and the kind of number a PSP merchant-success team can actually call on. The moat is also real: category peer medians and cross-merchant PSP-rail comparisons need data only the PSP holds, so this is not repackaged BI. But the commercial picture underneath is much thinner than the demo. 53.1% of that flagship 116.5bn sits in one merchant (M156, the default demo merchant); the median affected merchant has 29.8M IRR (~$30 over six months); and 18.5% of it (21.5bn across 23 merchants) sits where unverified money exceeds the merchant's entire realized GMV — M30 has ZERO verified revenue ever and still gets a confidence:high card for 3.98bn labelled "real amount, not an estimate" with a diagnosis that is provably wrong. Insight yield collapses at the cadence the product claims for itself: running zarin.insights.generate over all 343 merchants gives 22% empty feeds on the 6-month window, 50% at 30 days, and 79% at 7 days. And the whole merchant API is unauthenticated on the live deployment — 343 merchants' GMV, customers and row-level sessions readable by anyone, with Cache-Control: public.
lenses.not_higher_because: A live product that serves 343 merchants' revenue and per-session rows to anonymous callers cannot enter a PSP pilot at all — and the ops surface IS gated, so this is an omission, not an inability. Beyond that, the two things a buyer underwrites both fail verification: (a) the engagement story — PRODUCT.md says the merchant opens it weekly, but 270/343 merchants (79%) get an empty feed on a 7-day window and 172/343 (50%) at 30 days; (b) the money story — the flagship 147.3bn IRR opportunity on M156 is inflated ~44% by a peer baseline that includes M265, whose 94.4% no-attempt rate the project's own docs call a broken integration (peer median in-bank abandon 26.5% with it, 29.2% without; gap 8.76pp vs 6.07pp), and 18.5% of the headline unverified money carries a confidently-wrong diagnosis. There is also no metric anywhere — Control Center included — that tells the buyer what Zarbin is worth: it tracks latency, fallback rate and grounded rate, and feedback total is 0.
lenses.not_lower_because: The value numbers survive independent recomputation to the rial, not just to the headline: my own DuckDB query over data/marts/sessions.parquet produced 8,706 / 116,550,558,678 and /api/admin/platform returned exactly those digits. The differentiation is genuine and PSP-exclusive — no merchant-side tool can compute a category peer median or compare PSP-03 against PSP-04 on the same merchant's first attempts. The refusal discipline is implemented, not just documented: _apply_gmv_cap clamps estimates to realized GMV and converts zero-GMV merchants to alerts, gaps under 2pp emit no card, n_peers<8 forces low confidence, and both empty states are honest. The copilot answered «چرا فروشم کم شد؟» by correcting the premise ("your sales did not decline") and giving the LMDI decomposition — that is advisory behaviour, not a chart. And for the top 50 merchants by GMV, which carry 72% of platform volume, the engine produces cards for 94-96% of them at 30-day and 6-month cadence. That is a shippable operator tool for the segment that matters.
verified_strengths: The headline commercial number reproduces exactly. I computed platform paid_unverified independently from data/marts/sessions.parquet with DuckDB — 8,706 sessions, 116,550,558,678 IRR, settled_at non-null on 100% of them and verified_at null on 100% — and /api/admin/platform returned {"paid_unverified":8706,"paid_unverified_amount":116550558678}, the identical digits. The traceability claim holds for the number the business case rests on.

The moat is genuinely PSP-exclusive, not repackaged BI. /api/peers?m=M156 returns an exact-rank percentile against a named, rule-stated category cohort, and _card_psp_friction compares first attempts only across rails on the same merchant (PSP-03 20.8% vs PSP-04 60.8% on M156). Neither a merchant nor any merchant-side analytics tool can compute a cross-merchant peer median or a rail comparison — that data exists only inside the PSP.

The refusal discipline is implemented, not just claimed. I read _apply_gmv_cap: it clamps every rial estimate to realized GMV and converts cards on zero-GMV merchants into funnel alerts with impact 0 rather than publishing money; _gap_card returns None below a 2pp gap and forces confidence='low' under 8 peers. Running generate() across all 343 merchants, 201 of them get no rial-denominated opportunity at all — the engine really does decline to invent numbers on thin evidence.

The copilot exhibits advisory behaviour, not lookup. Asked «چرا فروشم کم شد؟» (a loaded premise) against M156 on the live deployment, it answered «فروش شما در این بازه کم نشده است» and then gave the LMDI decomposition of a +479.7bn IRR increase. Correcting the question is the thing a dashboard structurally cannot do.

For the segment that would actually be sold, coverage is strong. Across the top 50 merchants by GMV — which carry 72% of platform volume per the concentration figure I confirmed at top5_share=0.724 — generate() produces at least one card for 47/50 on the 6-month window and 48/50 on the last 30 days, versus 268/343 and 171/343 across the whole base.

findings.title: Every merchant's financials — including row-level sessions — are readable by anonymous callers on the live deployment
findings.location: https://zarbin-nine.vercel.app/api/meta, /api/overview, /api/customers, /api/evidence/sessions (zarin/api.py, no auth dependency on merchant routes)
findings.evidence: With no header of any kind: `urlopen('https://zarbin-nine.vercel.app/api/meta')` returned 343 merchants with GMV, total 5,165,464,690,799 IRR, and `Cache-Control: public, max-age=60`. `/api/overview?m=M18` returned {"gmv": 968621609500.0, "verified": 97718, "customers": 62176, "paid_unverified_amount": 7358260000.0}. `/api/evidence/sessions?m=M18` returned per-transaction rows: {"session_key": 1591590, "d": "2026-02-25", "amount": 599340000, "outcome": "verified", "win_psp": "PSP-04"}. The ops surface by contrast correctly required a signed session, so the capability to gate exists and was simply not applied to the merchant surface.
findings.impact: This is the single hard blocker to a pilot. A PSP cannot deploy a product that publishes its merchants' revenue, customer counts and transaction rows to the open internet — with a public CDN cache directive on top. Any merchant can read every competitor in its own category, which is exactly the data the peer-benchmarking feature is built on. docs/PLATFORM_BOOK.md §15 calls this a known limitation and says 'queries already scoped', but scope supplied by the caller is not tenancy.
findings.fix: Require the same signed session on /api/{meta,overview,insights,funnel,customers,peers,changes,evidence/*} that /api/admin/* already enforces, with the merchant_key bound to the token rather than read from the query string, and drop Cache-Control to private on those routes.

findings.title: At the weekly cadence the product claims for itself, 79% of merchants get an empty feed
findings.location: zarin/insights.py:660 generate(); PRODUCT.md ("محصولی که پذیرنده هر هفته باز می‌کند")
findings.evidence: Ran zarin.insights.generate over all 343 merchants at three windows (pipeline/_panel/biz_window.py): 6 months → 75/343 zero-card (22%), 538 cards; last 30d → 172/343 zero-card (50%), 300 cards; last 7d → 270/343 zero-card (79%), 98 cards. Restricted to the top 50 merchants by GMV: 3/50, 2/50, 23/50 zero-card respectively. Across all merchants on the 6-month window only 142/343 get any rial-denominated opportunity at all; median per-merchant opportunity is 0; the most common card is gmv_change (167 merchants), an alert with impact 0.
findings.impact: The product's stated retention model is a weekly habit, and that is what a per-merchant subscription would be underwritten against. A merchant who opens it weekly sees «فرصت قابل اتکایی پیدا نشد» four weeks out of five. The commercially honest positioning is a PSP-internal merchant-success tool for the top decile, not a merchant-facing weekly SaaS — but nothing in the product or docs makes that distinction, so a pilot would be scoped against an engagement number the engine cannot produce.
findings.fix: Either state the supported cadence honestly (monthly for the long tail, weekly only for high-volume merchants) or add cadence-appropriate content for quiet weeks — a 'nothing changed, here is your baseline' digest is a legitimate weekly artefact and costs one card generator.

findings.title: 18.5% of the headline unverified money carries a confidently-wrong diagnosis: merchants whose unverified total exceeds their entire realized revenue
findings.evidence: 23 of the 158 merchants with paid_unverified>0 have pua > their whole realized GMV, holding 21,505,478,359 IRR = 18.5% of the platform's 116,550,558,678. M48: gmv=1,400,000, pua=8,135,500,000 (5,811x); M30: gmv=0, pua=3,976,750,000; M136: gmv=0, pua=2,246,000,000. Raw check on M30: 69 of 84 sessions (82%) are paid_unverified and it has ZERO verified sessions across 2026-03-08..2026-06-29. generate('M30',...) still emits confidence='high', impact_low=impact_high=3976750000, capped=False, impact_label_fa='مبلغ واقعی در انتظار تعیین تکلیف (برآورد نیست)', diagnosis 'فراخوانی تایید (verify/callback) ... به نتیجه نرسیده است' and action 'لاگ خطای فراخوانی verify را ... بررسی کنید'. M48 and M30 are rows #2 and #5 of the operator's default call list (/api/admin/merchants?sort=unverified).
findings.impact: An ops rep works the call list top-down and tells a merchant with 1.4M IRR of lifetime revenue that it has 8.1bn IRR awaiting disposition, then advises it to check its verify timeout logs. The real situation — 'your verify integration has never worked once' — is a different conversation with a different owner and 10x the urgency. First contact with a real merchant destroys the product's credibility, and it happens on the second row of the list. The amount exemption from the GMV cap is defensible (it is settled money); the unconditioned diagnosis and action are not.
findings.fix: Branch _card_paid_unverified on the ratio: when paid_unverified_amount > realized GMV or the verified count is 0, retitle it as a never-completed integration, drop the 'check your logs' action for 'your verify callback has never succeeded — onboarding/integration review', and tag the row in /api/admin/merchants so the operator sees which conversation to have.

findings.title: The flagship 147bn IRR opportunity is inflated ~44% by a peer baseline containing a merchant the project itself documents as broken
findings.location: zarin/peers.py:30 peer_group (level='category' fallback has no health filter); zarin/insights.py:109 _gap_card; card inbank_gap on /api/insights?m=M156
findings.evidence: /api/peers?m=M156 returns n=5, level='category', rule 'همه پذیرندگان فعال هم‌صنف شما (دست‌کم ۵۰۰ جلسه)'. Those 5 peers have GMV 4.36bn–162.7bn against M156's 1,951bn — 12x to 448x smaller. One of them is M265, which PRODUCT.md itself lists as «بالاترین انصراف پیش از پرداخت (۹۴٪ — الگوی یکپارچه‌سازی خراب)». Measured from the parquet: M265 no_attempt=94.4%, so its inbank_abandon_rate is 3.65% purely because almost nobody reaches the bank. Peer median in-bank abandon WITH M265 = 0.2651; WITHOUT = 0.2920. M156's rate = 0.3527, so the gap is 8.76pp vs 6.07pp — a 44% inflation. _gap_card multiplies the gap linearly (excess_sessions = gap × sessions), so impact_mid 147,329,650,992 IRR would be roughly 102bn on the clean baseline.
findings.impact: This is the largest rial number the merchant workspace shows and the one a PSP would quote in a business case. It is inflated by including a structurally broken merchant whose brokenness biases the baseline in precisely the direction that enlarges the claim. The card carries confidence='low' and a small-peer-group warning, but nothing discloses that the baseline is a different order of magnitude or that one member's funnel is dead upstream.
findings.fix: Exclude merchants from the peer pool whose attempt_rate is degenerate (e.g. no_attempt_rate > 0.5) for any downstream rate benchmark — a merchant whose payers never reach the bank cannot be a baseline for a bank-page metric. One WHERE clause in POOL_SQL, applied per-metric.

findings.title: A merchant-facing card names PSP-03 as "noticeably weaker" when PSP-03 is one of the platform's stronger rails
findings.location: zarin/insights.py:406 _card_psp_friction (title_fa names worst['psp_code']); card psp_friction on /api/insights?m=M156
findings.evidence: The M156 card reads «درگاه PSP-03 به‌طور محسوس ضعیف‌تر از بقیه عمل می‌کند» off 1,511 first tries at 20.8%. Platform-wide first-try success by rail, computed from attempts.parquet: PSP-03 0.6025 over 691,091 first tries across 239 merchants; PSP-01 0.6050; PSP-04 0.6291; PSP-06 0.6373; PSP-05 0.4088; PSP-08 0.2419. Across the 59 merchants with ≥200 first tries on PSP-03 the median rate is 0.661 and M156 (0.208) is the 3rd worst. So PSP-03 is mid-pack platform-wide and M156's result is a merchant-local artefact.
findings.impact: The buyer is the PSP whose rail is being named. Merchant-facing copy that tells 59 merchants their gateway is weak — when that gateway runs at the platform average — is a positioning problem for the seller and a support-ticket generator ('move me off PSP-03'). The product holds the platform baseline that would make the claim precise and does not use it.
findings.fix: Title the card on the merchant's own routing rather than the rail ('your traffic on PSP-03 underperforms your other rails'), and add one sentence of platform context from the data already in attempts.parquet: 'PSP-03 averages 60% across the platform, so this is specific to your terminal.'

findings.title: The degenerate-rail guard silently suppresses the most rerouteable defect in the dataset
findings.location: zarin/insights.py:426 — rows = [r for r in rows if r["ok_rate"] >= 0.05 and r["successes"] >= 30]
findings.evidence: M27 sends 8,019 first attempts to PSP-03 with literally 0 successes (query over attempts.parquet: merchant_key='M27', psp_code='PSP-03', try_seq=1 → n=8,019, sum(ok)=0). Those sessions are forced to retry: 7,978 have n_tries=2, and win_psp shows 5,286 landing on PSP-05, 571 on PSP-02, 427 on PSP-04, with 1,735 (21.6%) never winning at all. generate('M27',...) returns only ['paid_unverified','gmv_change'] — no card of any kind names the dead rail, because the 0.05 floor drops it before the comparison. Two other merchants match: M273/PSP-05 (988 first tries, 0 successes) and M300/PSP-03 (529, 0).
findings.impact: The GMV cost is modest (I checked: PSP-03-first sessions still convert at 78.3% vs 81.0% elsewhere, so only ~217 sessions and ~375M IRR are actually lost), but 7,978 forced retries is the clearest routing action in the whole dataset and the one thing only the PSP can fix. The guard's stated rationale — don't manufacture a phantom rial opportunity — is right; the consequence, saying nothing at all, is not, and it removes the single most defensible 'we found something your own dashboards missed' story for a PSP demo.
findings.fix: Keep the 0.05 floor for choosing the comparison baseline, but emit a separate alert card when a rail has ≥200 first tries and <1% success — impact expressed as forced retries and unconverted sessions, not rials. Surface the same pattern platform-wide in the Control Center.

findings.title: Nothing in the product tells the buyer what the product is worth
findings.evidence: /api/admin/platform returns kpis (merchants, sessions, gmv, conv, no_attempt_rate, paid_unverified, recovered) plus two insights: unverified money and revenue concentration. /api/admin/performance returns latency/error/throughput only. /api/admin/ai-ops returns fallback_rate 0.1797, grounded_rate 0.8203, cost 0.0, and "feedback":{"total":0,"useful":0,"not_useful":0}. No endpoint reports opportunity surfaced across the base, opportunity acted on, merchants engaged, or any before/after outcome. I summed the per-merchant opportunity myself — 804,560,187,675 IRR mid across 343 merchants, 15.6% of platform GMV, with 71% of it in four merchants (M156, M31, M250, M33) — a number the product never computes.
findings.impact: A PSP renewal decision needs one line: 'Zarbin surfaced X rial of opportunity, merchants acted on Y, Z rial of unverified money was recovered.' The Control Center answers 'is Zarbin up?' rather than 'is Zarbin worth it?'. Declining to publish the 804bn aggregate is defensible (it is not credible as a headline), but the absence of any value metric leaves procurement with nothing to underwrite.
findings.fix: Add a value panel to /api/admin/platform: total opportunity by confidence tier, paid_unverified trend period-over-period as the one hard-money outcome, and a card-viewed / feedback funnel. The telemetry store already records intents and surfaces; the aggregation is a few lines over existing data.

findings.title: The Control Center reports the financial source of truth as last refreshed in 2018 while serving 2026 data
findings.evidence: Live /api/admin/sources returns {"id":"zarinpal",...,"is_truth":true,"freshness":"2018-10-20T01:46:40+00:00"}. That is epoch 1540000000 — Vercel's normalised build-artifact mtime — while the mart's max(d) is 2026-06-30 and the local file mtime is 2026-08-22T05:41:56Z. So the value is a deploy artefact of using file mtime as a data-recency proxy.
findings.impact: 'How fresh is the data?' is the first question a PSP ops team asks of a financial source, and the panel built to answer it is off by 7.8 years on the deployment a judge or a pilot customer will actually open. It also teaches the operator to ignore that field.
