(1) Code: `_card_change_alert` (zarin/insights.py:543-585) is the only one of the nine generators with no sample-size gate — the other eight all gate on MIN_SESSIONS_INSIGHT=100 or MIN_CUSTOMERS_RETENTION=50 (lines 246, 256, 267, 270, 308, 319, 348, 388, 415) and even the last-resort fallback gates at MIN_SIGNAL_SESSIONS=10 (line 499) — and it hardcodes `"confidence": "high"` (line 580). (2) Live: GET /api/insights?m=M336 returns exactly one card, gmv_change, `"confidence":"high"`, `"n":2`, "رشد ۱۸٪ فروش" with the causal diagnosis «بیشترین دلیل این تغییر «مبلغ متوسط تراکنش» بوده است» — one session in each 90-day half. The frontend renders `<ConfChip level="high">` as a green "اطمینان بالا" chip (frontend/src/components/ui.tsx:61-65) directly beside "نمونه: ۲", and /api/meta lists all 343 merchants including M336 (2 sessions), so that dashboard is reachable. (3) Statistics: my own permutation over the card's exact split — 167 alerted merchants, 400 draws, days shuffled between halves, alert-firing condition copied from the code including the `decomposable` predicate — gives median P(fire | no-trend null) = 0.76 (identical to the claim) with 90% of alerts firing ≥50% of the time under that null; day-level bootstrap of the argmax driver gives median reproduction 0.72 and 47% below 0.70 (claim: 0.76 / 45%). Per-merchant it matches: M186 p_null=1.00 boot=0.23, M134 0.93, M85 0.94, M272 0.95. My census of the alert population reproduces 167 alerts, 60 with n<100, 29 with n<30 (claim said 28), 11 with n<15, smallest n=2 (M336) and 3 (M253). The defect is also BROADER than the location given: zarin/copilot.py:_ans_changes (line ~232) returns the same decomposition with a hardcoded "high" and no n gate, and unlike the card it never prints the sample size at all — locally, copilot.answer('M336','چرا فروشم کم شد؟',...) returns confidence "high" with "بزرگ‌ترین عامل: «مبلغ متوسط»" on two sessions. Where I do push back is severity. "critical" in this rubric means wrong money, a security hole, or a claim false in a way that misleads. No money is wrong here: impact_low/impact_high are 0, the card is card_type "alert" (so `_score` zeroes it and the sort in generate() ranks every opportunity above it — on M156 it is card 4 of 4), and risk_gmv is the realized GMV delta, not an estimate. Every number it states is arithmetically true and traceable — for M336 the LMDI attribution to "ticket" is a tautology, not noise (1 session vs 1 session means the only thing that can differ IS the amount) — and the evidence drawer exposes n=2, both periods, the SQL and the method. What is genuinely wrong is the label and the advice: a green "high confidence" statistical badge and a "keep this product/price mix" action derived from n=1 vs n=1, with no caveat in the registry entry for gmv_decomposition (`"caveats": []`). Also mildly overstated: "the loudest thing on the merchant dashboard" — alerts are deliberately sorted last; it is only the loudest thing for merchants where it is the ONLY card, which is precisely the low-n merchants where the other generators correctly gated out (without it M336's dashboard would be empty). That is a real and unflattering defect worth fixing (gate at MIN_SESSIONS_INSIGHT, or downgrade confidence and drop the driver sentence below ~100 sessions, in both insights.py and copilot.py), but it is high, not critical.

confirmed.title: Amount quintiles are equal-count over tied prices: 84 published bands have lo==hi, and four "amount bands" containing the identical price report four different conversion rates
confirmed.evidence: ntile(5) OVER (ORDER BY amount, session_key) splits by row count, so tied amounts straddle boundaries. Live and local, M106's published amount_bands: band2 lo=hi=100000 conv=0.7089, band3 lo=hi=100000 conv=0.6888, band4 lo=hi=100000 conv=0.6945, band5 lo=hi=100000 conv=0.7277 — a 3.9pp spread across four bands whose amount is a single constant, produced entirely by the session_key tiebreaker. Live GET /api/funnel?m=M250 (Server-Timing: app;dur=784.9) returns band1 30001–429000 conv 0.4595, band2 429000–429000 conv 0.5710, band3 429000–759000 conv 0.5011: the price 429,000 occupies three of five bands, and 687,170 of 1,055,912 sessions (65%) carry an amount that straddles a boundary (M31: 170,943/312,814 = 55%). Repo-wide: 84 published bands with lo==hi, and 130 of 343 merchants have at least one adjacent pair sharing a boundary value. The tied sessions themselves convert identically across bands (M250 amount=429000: 0.5705 / 0.5710 / 0.5750), confirming the split carries no amount information.
confirmed.fix: Build bands on distinct amount values rather than row rank — e.g. quantile_cont over amount to get cut points, then bucket by value with ties kept whole (width_bucket or a CASE over the cut points), dropping any band whose lo==hi or which collapses into its neighbour. Merge collapsed bands before publishing and label the merged range.
confirmed.verdict: I could not refute this; every number in it reproduces exactly, locally and on the live deployment, and the impact is worse than stated in one respect. `ntile(5) OVER (ORDER BY amount, session_key)` in zarin/analytics.py:112 and zarin/insights.py:311 is equal-count over a total order, so tied prices straddle boundaries. M106 returns four published bands with lo=hi=100000 and conversions 0.7089/0.6888/0.6945/0.7277 (identical live: app;dur=52.2); M250 live (app;dur=1261.9) puts the price 429,000 in three of five bands, with 687,170/1,055,912 = 65.1% of its sessions straddling (M31 54.6%), and the tied sessions at 429,000 convert 0.5705/0.5710/0.5750 — the split carries no amount information. Repo-wide: 667 published bands, 84 with lo==hi, 130 merchants with an adjacent boundary-sharing pair. The reviewer's "130 of 343" actually understates it: only 134 merchants publish any band at MIN_SEGMENT_N, so it is 130/134 = 97%. I extended the check to money, which the finding only asserts: high_value_friction fires for 24 merchants at n_top>=100, and for 10 of them more than 20% of the "top amount quintile" sits at a price also present in bands 2-4 — M140 has 328/373 (88%) of its top quintile at exactly 9,900,000, which is also band4's max, and publishes 140,833,465–281,666,929 IRR; M312 has 81% overlap, publishes 3,666,696–7,333,392 IRR on a claimed 11.1pp gap, and under a tie-respecting split (each distinct amount wholly in one band) its gap is −0.142 — the top quintile converts 14.2pp BETTER and the card should not fire. M319 (769,040,000 IRR), M140, M161 and M209 do not even have five well-defined quintiles under a tie-respecting split. Two minor corrections that do not change the verdict: lo==hi alone is not proof of an arbitrary split (a price holding >20% of volume forces a degenerate band under any quantile method — 74 flat bands survive a tie-respecting split, so the true signature is adjacent bands sharing a value, not flatness), and the Persian note «تا اثر ترکیب پذیرنده‌ها حذف شود» claims within-merchant construction against merchant-mix confounding, which is true, so citing it as the false promise is a stretch. Severity high is right, not inflated and not critical: no settled money is misstated and each band's rate is arithmetically correct for the rows in it, but a published opportunity card puts a rial range on a comparison whose direction reverses when ties are respected, and the funnel table shows a merchant four rows labelled "۱۰۰٬۰۰۰ ریال تا ۱۰۰٬۰۰۰ ریال" with four different conversion rates. Nothing in docs records this as a known residual — ZB-120 requested exactly this tiebreaker and is marked fixed.

confirmed.title: Response cache answers merchant routes before the auth dependency, leaking another tenant's money (defeats the recorded ZB-001/ZB-030 fix)
confirmed.location: zarin/cache.py:92-100 (middleware) vs zarin/api.py:36-37 (registration order) and zarin/api.py:121 (_merchant_scope)
confirmed.evidence:
docs/EXPERT_REVIEW.md:335 and :364 record ZB-001 and ZB-030 as "✅ fixed". They are not, in the mode the fix exists for. Repro at pipeline/_panel/rel_authcache.py with ZARIN_REQUIRE_AUTH=1:
  1 no-auth cold  -> 401
  2 no-auth warm  -> 200 HIT public, max-age=60, s-maxage=31536000, stale-while-revalidate=86400
  3 M156 tok->M18 -> 200 gmv: 968621609500.0
One authorised fetch fills the LRU; the next request with NO Authorization header at all gets 200 with the full KPI payload, and an M156-scoped token reads M18's 968,621,609,500 IRR GMV. cache.middleware is registered at api.py:36 (inner) and short-circuits on hit before FastAPI ever evaluates Depends(_merchant_scope) — exactly the hazard cache.py's own comment says it avoided for /api/admin/* ("the operator gate runs in the route's dependencies, i.e. *after* this middleware"). The comment names the bug and then leaves it open on the merchant routes. Worse, the leaked body ships Cache-Control: public, s-maxage=31536000, so any CDN in front caches one tenant's financials publicly for a year on a URL-only key. `grep -n 'REQUIRE_AUTH|cache.clear|CACHEABLE' tests/` returns no matches: 180 passing tests never exercise this mode or this middleware.
confirmed.fix: Key the cache on the authenticated principal, or skip the cache entirely when REQUIRE_AUTH is on. Minimal: in cache.middleware, `if REQUIRE_AUTH: return await call_next(request)` before the CACHEABLE check, and set `Cache-Control: private, no-store` for merchant routes in that mode. Add the three-line test from pipeline/_panel/rel_authcache.py.
confirmed.verdict: Not refuted — the mechanism, the repro sequence and the exact leaked GMV all reproduce, and the real blast radius is larger than claimed. `cache.middleware` is registered first at api.py:36 and therefore runs innermost, closest to the router, so a `_get(key)` hit at cache.py:104 returns a `Response` before FastAPI ever evaluates `Depends(_merchant_scope)`. The key is `path?query` only (cache.py:102); the Authorization header is not in it and no `Vary` is emitted. One authorised fetch of any of the nine CACHEABLE routes therefore makes that URL readable by anyone with no header at all, by a garbage token, and by a valid token scoped to a different merchant — I confirmed all three, and my own cold-cache control returns the correct 403, proving the dependency is sound and the cache is what defeats it. Beyond the reviewer's single `/api/overview` case, `/api/evidence/sessions`, `/api/customers`, `/api/peers`, `/api/funnel`, `/api/insights` and `/api/changes` all return byte-identical bodies to the unauthenticated and wrong-tenant callers; `/api/copilot`, excluded from CACHEABLE for an unrelated telemetry reason, still 401s correctly, which isolates the cause precisely. The CDN half also holds and is independent of the LRU: cache.py:117-119 stamps `public, s-maxage=31536000` on any 200, MISS included, so a REQUIRE_AUTH=1 deploy publishes one tenant's financials to the shared edge on the first authorised request — and I verified Vercel is in fact edge-caching these URLs today (`X-Vercel-Cache: HIT`, `Age: 31`). The irony the reviewer identifies is real and verifiable in the repo: memory.md:59 records this exact middleware-before-guard hazard as an invariant, enumerates `/api/copilot` and `/api/admin/*`, and stops there. Two things in the finding are wrong and should be corrected on the ticket. First, the citation: memory.md's "Important env vars" section does not list ZARIN_REQUIRE_AUTH, and neither does the DEPLOY_VERCEL.md production recipe — the flag is documented only in config.py and api.py docstrings, so "the documented production switch" overstates it. Second, nothing is leaking on the live deployment right now: it runs with REQUIRE_AUTH off, where merchant data is intentionally public and disclosed as a demo limitation, and the shipped SPA cannot even authenticate in the enforced mode (Login.tsx:97 omits merchant_key, which api.py:237 400s). Neither correction touches the defect. I still rate it critical rather than high, on the brief's own bar of "a claim that is false in a way that misleads": ZARIN_REQUIRE_AUTH=1 is the entire substance of the recorded ZB-001/ZB-030 fixes, docs/EXPERT_REVIEW.md publishes both as ✅ fixed, and in the only mode where that fix does anything, authentication is a no-op on nine endpoints after a single warm request — with zero tests anywhere in tests/ that would ever notice.

confirmed.title: Anonymous callers can evict the request-telemetry ring and inflate the operator response 200x; "attention" is blind to 4xx
confirmed.location: zarin/obs.py:19 (record uses raw request.url.path), obs.py:22 (_trackable), obs.py:80-88 (attention rules)
confirmed.evidence:
Repro pipeline/_panel/rel_cardinality.py — 3000 unauthenticated GETs to /api/xxxx<i>:
  ring=3001 endpoint_rows=3001 error_rate=0.0 client_error_rate=0.9997 attention=0 resp_bytes=389184
The path is recorded verbatim and unbounded, so 3000 anonymous 404s produce 3001 rows in /api/admin/performance and a 389 KB response (baseline ~2 KB); at the ring's maxlen=8000 that is ~1 MB re-sorted and shipped on every operator page load, and all real telemetry is evicted. Confirmed live, not just locally: the deployed /api/admin/performance endpoints table contains a row {"path":"/api/nonexistent","count":1,"error_rate":0.0} from one of my probes. Separately, with 99.97% of requests failing 4xx the dashboard reports error_rate 0.0 and attention=[] — obs.py:81-87 only escalates on status>=500 or p95>1500, so an endpoint 4xx-ing on 100% of calls looks perfectly healthy.
confirmed.fix: Bucket unmatched paths: in obs.record, replace the raw path with the matched route template (`request.scope.get("route").path`) and fall back to a single "<unmatched>" label. Add a per-endpoint client_error_rate to obs.summary and one attention rule for it (>0.5 sustained).
confirmed.verdict: I could not refute this; it reproduces exactly as described and I confirmed it on the live deployment with my own unauthenticated probes. Both halves are real and independent. (a) Cardinality: `record()` stores `request.url.path` verbatim and `_trackable()` admits any string under `/api/`, so any anonymous caller mints one permanent row per invented path in the operator's Product Performance table — 60 curl calls with no token produced 60 junk rows live (1640 B → 6315 B), and at the ring's maxlen=8000 I measured a 639 KB response costing 114 ms of server time, with all genuine telemetry evicted (`overview_row_survives: False`). The frontend maps the array with no slice, so that is also 8000 DOM rows. This is the textbook unbounded-label-cardinality bug, and the fix is one line — key on `request.scope["route"].path` (the route template) and bucket unmatched paths as a single `<unmatched>` row. (b) 4xx blindness: per-endpoint `error_rate` counts only `status >= 500` (obs.py:74) and `attention` escalates only on that or p95 > 1500 (obs.py:85-88), so an endpoint 4xx-ing on 100% of calls reports error_rate 0.0 and raises nothing — I measured `client_error_rate=1.0, attention=[]`. Worse than claimed, actually: `client_error_rate` IS computed at obs.py:95 but no component renders it (only the type exists, api.ts:109), while the visible tile is bound to the 5xx-only `error_rate`. For a payments integration surface, where the realistic client-contract break is a wall of 400/422, this is the exact failure mode the dashboard is blind to. Two corrections to the write-up, neither of which moves the severity: the saturated payload is 639 KB, not "~1 MB" (~1.6x overstated), and the bloated response is served only to an authenticated operator, so this is operator-side degradation and observability blinding, not attacker-pullable bandwidth amplification — the "200x" figure is nonetheless conservative (live baseline 1640 B vs saturated 639 KB is ~390x). One genuine mitigation the reviewer did not mention: store.py's docstring declares this "deliberately the *hackathon* store" with a documented OTel/ClickHouse migration path, and durable=False means the ring is per-lambda and ephemeral — but that excuses the storage choice, not route normalisation (one line, every APM does it) and not the 4xx rule, which has nothing to do with the store. High is the right band: it is not critical (no wrong money, no auth bypass, no false product claim), and not medium (anonymous, unauthenticated, zero-cost, live-confirmed, and it defeats the only request-observability surface the product ships).

confirmed.title: Control Center performance telemetry is a per-instance in-memory ring and is blind to every CDN hit
confirmed.evidence: Immediately after issuing 60+ API calls to the live deployment (8 endpoints cold, 6 sequential origin hits, 24 concurrent fan-out, 3 copilot calls), GET /api/admin/performance returned `{"total":40,"throughput_rps":0.16,"latency_ms":{"p50":35.4,"p95":222.4,"p99":512.9}}` and an endpoints list containing only /api/overview (24), /api/copilot (3), /api/admin/copilot (3), /api/admin/sources (3), /api/admin/ai-ops (6), /api/admin/merchants (1). There is no row at all for /api/meta, /api/insights, /api/funnel, /api/customers, /api/peers, /api/quality or /api/evidence/sessions, every one of which I called against that host.
confirmed.fix: Either label the panel as per-instance in the UI and the API payload (cheap, honest), or push request events to a shared store; and count CDN-served traffic separately so the dashboard does not silently equate 'origin requests' with 'traffic'.
confirmed.verdict: I could not refute the mechanism — it reproduces, and my evidence is cleaner than the original's. Two independent losses are proven by controlled A/B, not inferred: 8 CDN-HIT requests to /api/meta produced zero telemetry rows while 8 cache-busted MISSes to the identical endpoint produced exactly 8; and 20 concurrent requests that all returned `x-vercel-cache: MISS` (all 20 provably reached the function) were reported as 5 by /api/admin/performance, twice in a row. I also watched the ring read 121 and then 1 on consecutive calls. So the surface that answers "how is Zarbin itself doing?" is showing one lambda's slice of origin-only traffic, and nothing in the JSON or the UI says so. What I do refute is two parts of the framing. First, "not labelled as samples" is only true of the product: docs/EVALUATION.md:221 names this limitation explicitly ("Telemetry is per-instance and non-durable on serverless… show what the warm instance has seen") and DEPLOYMENT_SPEC.md:68 names the fix, so this is a disclosed, ticketed ceiling rather than an unnoticed one — the real gap is that the disclosure never reaches the operator looking at the tiles. Second, the impact direction is stated too broadly. Only `total` and `throughput_rps` are structurally under-reported; excluding CDN hits removes the *fastest* successful requests, so p50/p95/p99 are biased pessimistic and error_rate is biased high — the dashboard never flatters itself on speed or stability, which is the direction that would actually mislead an operator into inaction. Also worth noting the author did think about the adjacent trap: api.py:34-37 deliberately registers obs outside cache so the in-process LRU hits are still counted, with a comment saying exactly why. Severity: medium, not high. It is a real defect with a real consequence — the ops copilot repeats a 5-of-20 sample as platform fact at confidence="high" — but it touches no money, no security and no merchant-facing number; it is self-referential telemetry, its bias on the quality metrics is conservative, and it is already written down as a known serverless limitation with a named migration. The cheap fix is one honest field (`scope: "instance"`, plus a line of UI copy and a "origin only — CDN-served requests not counted" note), not a Postgres migration.

confirmed.title: Ops copilot has no refusal path — every unmatched question returns the platform status line at confidence=high
confirmed.evidence:
Live, with an ops session token, three unrelated questions to /api/admin/copilot returned identical intent=system, confidence=high:
  Q "وضعیت پلتفرم چطور است؟" -> "وضعیت کلی: ۳۴۳ پذیرندهٔ فعال…"
  Q "کدام پذیرنده بیشترین پول تاییدنشده دارد؟" -> "وضعیت کلی: ۳۴۳ پذیرندهٔ فعال…" (names no merchant)
  Q "چه کاری باید انجام بدم؟" -> "وضعیت کلی: ۳۴۳ پذیرندهٔ فعال…"
Reading zarin/ops_copilot.py: _plan() is 8 regexes and then an unconditional `return _system(f, t)`. There is no clarify/unrecognised branch and no retrieval layer — the merchant side got nlu.py (522 lines, calibrated by pipeline/calibrate_nlu.py, evaluated by zarin.ai.eval.retrieval); the ops side got none of it, while its docstring claims "Same two-stage contract as the merchant copilot".
confirmed.fix: Add an unrecognised branch before the catch-all: if no regex matched, return confidence="low" with the list of ops intents it can answer (mirroring copilot.py's clarify plan). Route the merchant-naming questions to control.merchants() with the existing sort keys.
confirmed.verdict: I could not refute it — it reproduces exactly, in code and live, and it is if anything understated. `zarin/ops_copilot.py:_plan()` is a chain of first-match-wins regexes ending in an unconditional `return _system(f, t)` at line 117 (the 9th branch, `(کل سیستم|سیستم|پلتفرم|همه‌چیز|وضعیت کلی)` at line 114, is therefore dead-equivalent to the fallback — a trivial correction to the reviewer's "8 regexes", which does not change the substance). There is no out_of_scope / clarify / low-confidence branch anywhere in the 155-line module, and `tests/test_ops_copilot_routing.py` — the test file added for ZB-044 — parametrizes all 9 intents and the no-data paths but contains no unmatched/refusal case, so the gap is not merely untested, it is unimplemented. Live against the deployment with an ops token, all four probes (including the reviewer's exact three) returned `intent=system, confidence=high` with the identical «وضعیت کلی: ۳۴۳ پذیرندهٔ فعال…» line. Three things make it worse than claimed, not better. (1) It is not limited to adjacent-but-unhandled questions: «قیمت بیت‌کوین چقدر است؟» — nothing to do with payments — also returns the platform status at confidence=high with `grounded=true` and `note_fa` "این پاسخ مستقیماً از موتور تحلیلی قطعی می‌آید؛ همه اعداد قابل ردیابی‌اند". (2) The asymmetry with the merchant side is stark and same-repo: `copilot.answer('M156','قیمت بیت کوین چند است؟')` returns `out_of_scope / low` with a proper decline, and it even answers «چه کاری باید انجام بدم؟» usefully (`priorities`) and the unverified-money question (`paid_unverified`, ۹۱۲ sessions / ۶۱٫۸ میلیارد ریال). (3) The Control Center's own «ایمنی در نبود داده» bar (frontend/src/ops/OpsAI.tsx:72) currently reads `refusal_safety: 1.0` live, but `zarin/ai/eval/runner.py:23` runs every case through `copilot.answer` (merchant) only — so the surface displays a 100% refusal-safety score for a property the copilot on that very page does not have. That is the exact defect the project logged as ZB-040 ("Refusal safety 100% is vacuous"), rated HIGH, whose verifier explicitly wrote "I'd keep it high"; it was fixed on the merchant side via nlu.py and never ported to the ops side. The reviewer's "answerable one endpoint away" is also verified: `/api/admin/merchants?sort=unverified` returns rows sorted by `paid_unverified_amount` desc (M156, 61,847,264,950 rial). Severity high is right by the project's own precedent; I considered medium (ops-scope-gated internal surface, no wrong merchant-facing money, the numbers returned are true — just for a different question) but the free-text hero page «از سلامت محصول بپرس», the docstring claim "Same two-stage contract as the merchant copilot" (line 3), and the vacuous 100% safety bar sitting on the same page keep it at high. Note: repo HEAD is 16ba370, not the 5acf9e1 named in the brief; I judged HEAD plus the live deployment.

confirmed.title: Merchant copilot answers "how much money did I lose?" with total successful sales, at confidence=high
confirmed.location: zarin/nlu.py:375 (gmv intent anchor "چقدر پول", weighted x4)
confirmed.evidence: Offline and live agree. `copilot.route_detail('چقدر پول از دست دادم؟')` returns `('gmv', 'search')`; `copilot.answer('M156', 'چقدر پول از دست دادم؟', ...)` returns intent=gmv, confidence=high, answer "در این بازه ۵۵٬۹۴۰ جلسهٔ پرداخت ثبت شد و ۳۰٬۵۰۸ پرداخت به تایید رسید؛ فروش موفق ۱٫۹۵ هزار میلیارد ریال…". Live /api/copilot?m=M156 gives the identical answer. Three near-synonyms behave correctly (چقدر فروش از دست دادم؟ / ضرر من چقدر بوده؟ / چقدر درآمد از دست رفته دارم؟ all -> intent=clarify, confidence=low with suggestions), so this is one anchor, not a systemic router failure: the literal string "چقدر پول" is a gmv anchor and matches the question verbatim.
confirmed.fix: Narrow the gmv anchor from "چقدر پول" to "چقدر پول گرفتم"/"چقدر پول رسید", and add "چقدر پول از دست دادم" to the priorities intent examples in nlu.py. Re-run `python -m zarin.ai.eval.retrieval -v` to confirm no regression.
confirmed.verdict: I could not refute this. It reproduces exactly as described, offline and against the live deployment, at a commit LATER than the one it was filed against — `route_detail('چقدر پول از دست دادم؟')` returns `('gmv','search')` and the answer comes back `intent=gmv, confidence=high` with the quoted successful-sales summary and zero suggestions; live `/api/copilot` returns the identical payload in 6.3ms of server time. The root cause is precisely where the claimant put it: `zarin/nlu.py:375` registers the literal `"چقدر پول"` as a gmv anchor at 4x weight, while `"از دست دادن"` is only a friction anchor (line 356), and gmv wins 0.1507 to 0.1330 — clearing the ACCEPT threshold of 0.13 by 0.02. Two things make it worse than filed. First, the blast radius is bigger, not smaller, than "one anchor, one phrasing": `چقدر پول سوخت؟` routes to gmv at 0.190 — a *higher* score than the question tested — and `چقدر پول نرسید به من؟`, `چقدر پول از دست میدهم؟` and `چقدر پول رو از دست دادم؟` all route to gmv too, and the eval set has no gold case for this family at all (one `از دست` case, gold `recovery`), so the published 3.2%/2.2% misroute rates never covered it. Second, two safeguards that should have caught it are inert: `confidence` is a hard-coded per-plan constant (`copilot.py:396`) reflecting data sufficiency rather than routing certainty, so every routed answer gets a high badge; and `Match.margin`, computed with the comment "a low margin is real ambiguity", is never read by any Python code — the UI's ZB-032 "I didn't understand you" admission (`Copilot.tsx:135`) fires only for `fallback`/`out_of_scope`, so a confident misroute is indistinguishable from a correct answer. The one place the claim overreaches is wording: "revenue earned reported as if it were revenue lost" implies a mislabelled number, and there is none — the answer correctly calls its figures `فروش موفق`. It is a confident non-sequitur, not wrong money, which is why this is high and not critical. The impact statement otherwise checks out: `priorities` genuinely computes the answer the merchant wanted (61.8B rials real unverified settled + 147.3B capped opportunity, properly caveated) and never gets reached. Product claim 7 — "the copilot answers the question that was asked, or refuses and says why" — is falsified on a natural, commercially central phrasing.

confirmed.title: LLM polish rewrites the answer's TIME FRAME, so a 6-month total is shown to the merchant as "yesterday's sales" — with اطمینان بالا
confirmed.evidence: Typed «دیروز چقدر فروختم» into the live composer in Chrome (390px, real login flow). The bubble rendered: «دیروز ۵۵٬۹۴۰ جلسه پرداخت ثبت شد و ۳۰٬۵۰۸ پرداخت تایید یافت. فروش موفق ۱٫۹۵ هزار میلیارد ریال بود…» with chips «با کمک هوش مصنوعی» + «اطمینان بالا». The deterministic answer it replaced says «در این بازه…». Hitting /api/copilot/polish?m=M156 15 times over 5 time-scoped questions: 8 fabricated a period — «دیروز چقدر فروختم» 1/3, «امروز چقدر فروختم» 2/3, «این هفته چقدر فروختم» 2/3, «دیروز چند تا مشتری داشتم» 3/3 — every one returned source=llm, grounded=true, confidence=high/medium, quality_flags=[]. Of the 9 calls the guard let through, 8 carried a wrong period. grounding_failure() checks forbidden payloads, length, numeric value+unit tracing, assertion/polarity markers and a novel-word RATIO — a single inserted word like «دیروز» trips none of them.
confirmed.fix: Add a temporal-scope check to grounding_failure(): reject the rephrasing if it contains any period word (دیروز/امروز/این هفته/این ماه/امسال/…) that is absent from the deterministic text. Two lines next to the existing _UNITS check, and it reuses the same _norm/_WORD_RE machinery.
confirmed.verdict: CONFIRMED — I could not refute it, and my one apparent refutation turned out to be my own bug. First pass I probed with `curl -G --data-urlencode` from Git Bash and got `intent=out_of_scope` for all five questions, which would have killed the finding outright (Copilot.tsx:75 skips polish entirely for out_of_scope). That was Windows mangling the Persian query bytes, not the product: re-probing with `urllib.parse.urlencode(..., encoding="utf-8")` gives `intent=gmv, confidence=high` for «دیروز چقدر فروختم» on the live API. The mechanism is real and I isolated it in three independent ways. (1) Guard gap, offline: `grounding_failure("دیروز " + det, det)` returns `None` — as do «امروز», «این هفته», «در هفته گذشته». Prepending one time word inserts a single content word into an otherwise verbatim sentence, so the numeric tracer sees identical values/units, the marker lists (assertion + polarity) don't contain time words, `_unsupported_sentence` needs >=3 novel content words (`_SENT_NOVEL_MIN`, gateway.py:122), and the 0.85 novelty ratio is nowhere near. Nothing in gateway.py:206-240 models the time frame at all. (2) Live rate: 15 polish calls over 5 time-scoped questions → 8 returned `source=llm` and 7 of those 8 carried a fabricated period, all with `grounded=true`, `quality_flags=[]`, `fallback=false`, `confidence=high` (medium for the customers one). Reviewer said 8/15 and 8-of-9; I got 7/15 and 7-of-8 — same phenomenon, LLM sampling noise. The exact bubble they quote reproduced verbatim: «دیروز ۵۵٬۹۴۰ جلسهٔ پرداخت ثبت شد … فروش موفق ۱٫۹۵ هزار میلیارد ریال بود» where the engine wrote «در این بازه ۵۵٬۹۴۰ …». (3) UI path is live, not just the API: the deployed bundle /assets/index-LuObPBrS.js contains `polish:s=>Ct("copilot/polish",{m:e,q:s,f:t.f,t:t.t,surface:"merchant"})`, Copilot.tsx:80-82 swaps the text in whenever `source === "llm"`, and ui.tsx:62 maps high→«اطمینان بالا» — with the composer footer at Copilot.tsx:193 still promising «اعداد هرگز توسط هوش مصنوعی ساخته نمی‌شوند». Two things I'd add to their write-up rather than subtract. Aggravator: this is not purely an LLM defect — zarin/ai/eval/retrieval_cases.py:129 pins «کل فروش موفق دیروزم چند تومن شد» to intent `gmv` as the DESIRED routing, so the deterministic engine deliberately answers a "yesterday" question with a 6-month total hedged as «در این بازه». The model doesn't invent the mismatch, it removes the hedge and states it as fact. Mitigation, the only one: the evidence drawer does carry `period: 2026-01-01 تا 2026-06-30` and `params {'f':'2026-01-01','t':'2026-06-30'}` — but that is one click behind «این عدد از کجا آمد؟» and does not appear in the sentence the merchant reads. Severity holds at critical under this rubric's own definition ("a claim that is false in a way that misleads"): the digits are the engine's, but a merchant is told 1.95 trillion rial was sold yesterday when that is 181 days of revenue, under the highest-confidence badge, on a surface whose footer denies exactly this can happen. Cheapest root-cause fix is in the shared guard, not the caller: budget a small closed set of period words the way _POLARITY_MARKERS are budgeted (introduce = reject), since every polish path routes through grounding_failure().

confirmed.title: «اطمینان بالا» growth verdicts and prescriptive advice generated from 2–15 transactions, for 59 of 343 merchants
confirmed.evidence: _card_change_alert is the only one of the nine generators with no MIN_SESSIONS_INSIGHT (=100) gate — its only guards are n_days>=28 and |rel|>=0.10 — and it hardcodes "confidence": "high". Ran insights.generate() for all 343 merchants over 2026-01-01..2026-06-30: 59 merchants get gmv_change as their ONLY card while having <100 sessions, all at confidence "high". Examples: M336 n=2 «رشد ۱۸٪ فروش در نیمه دوم دوره», M253 n=3 «افت ۲۰٪», M134 n=11 «رشد ۷۰۰٪», M135 n=15 «رشد ۵۲۴٪». Rendered M336's overview in Chrome: one card, badge «اطمینان بالا», chip «نمونه: ۲», action «رشد از بزرگ‌تر شدن سبد خرید آمده — همین ترکیب محصول/قیمت را حفظ کنید». The trend chart draws a straight line between the merchant's only two sales (بهمن ۱۵ and خرداد ۶) as if it were a six-month trend.
confirmed.fix: Apply the same MIN_SESSIONS_INSIGHT floor the other eight generators use, or at minimum ladder the confidence the way the peer cards do (`"high" if n >= MIN_SESSIONS_INSIGHT else "low"`) and drop the prescriptive action_by_driver text below the floor.
confirmed.verdict: Refutation failed — the finding reproduces verbatim, including the exact count (59/343) and all four named merchants, and it reproduces on the live deployment at the default period, not just locally. I attacked it from four angles and none held. (a) "It's an alert, not an opportunity, so no money is published": true that `impact_high=0` suppresses the rial headline and the `impact_label_fa` line in InsightCard (both gated on `impact_high > 0`), but the observation, the causal diagnosis and the prescriptive action all render, under the same green chip-good «اطمینان بالا» used for evidence-backed cards. Mitigation, not a defence. (b) "The delta is realized GMV, not an estimate, so 'high' means 'measured, not inferred'": that reading is killed by the product's own tooltip, which defines the badge as «بر اساس حجم نمونه» and glosses it as «با خیال راحت اقدام کنید». By the product's own definition the label is false at n=2. (c) "Maybe the default period is shorter so these merchants wouldn't clear n_days>=28": the API's default period is the full 2026-01-01..2026-06-30, and the live no-parameter call returns the card. (d) "Already fixed / already recorded": HEAD is 16ba370, five commits past the 5acf9e1 under review, and the defect is still live in code and in production. Only two things in the claim are slightly loose, neither substantive: `_card_change_alert` is not the *only* generator without a MIN_SESSIONS_INSIGHT gate — `_card_paid_unverified` (insights.py:182) also lacks one, gating on `paid_unverified >= 5` instead, though that card reports counted, realized settled money so "high" is defensible there; and the confidence literal is at :585, not :586. Severity stays **high** and should not be raised to critical: no money is wrong (54.9M → 64.9M is genuinely +18.2%), nothing is fabricated, and no security surface is touched. It stays above medium because it is the sole, default, production experience for 17% of merchants, it inverts the product's own documented meaning of its top confidence label, the enclosing section explicitly promises the opposite, and the advice given is causal and prescriptive off a two-row sample whose "cause" is mathematically forced.

confirmed.verdict: The finding reproduces exactly, on both the current worktree (HEAD 16ba370, which is ahead of 5acf9e1) and the live Vercel deployment, and it is not recorded as fixed anywhere in docs/EXPERT_REVIEW_ISSUES.md (the nearest neighbours, ZB-047/ZB-107/ZB-108, are about peer dispersion and cohort/concentration floors, not the merchant's own n on the peers surface). Mechanism is precisely as located: C:\Users\pro\OneDrive\Desktop\zarinpal\zarin\peers.py:19 gates the peer pool at `sessions >= 500` and :76 gates in-period peers at `HAVING sum(sessions) >= 100`, but :89 `me = period_agg(m, f, t)` applies no floor whatsoever to the merchant being judged, and :117 `"low_n": len(vals) < 8` counts only peers — so with 11 peers the caution flag is False no matter how thin the merchant is. Live `/api/peers?m=M336` (Server-Timing app;dur=25.8) returns four rows with `"percentile": 100, "n_peers": 11, "low_n": false, "suppressed": false` and `group.me.sessions = 2`; p50 for conv is 0.68287, i.e. the claimed «میانه همتایان ۶۸٫۳٪», off two lifetime sessions. In frontend/src/pages/PeersPage.tsx:55 `strong = r.percentile >= 60` selects `chip-good`, whose token is `--good: #0a6f4d` (theme.css:26) — green — and the `chip-warn` «گروه کوچک — با احتیاط» at :62 is gated on `r.low_n`, so it never renders. The copilot half also reproduces: `copilot.answer('M244', 'با همتاهام چطورم؟', …)` returns intent=peers, confidence="high", «صدک ۱۰۰ از ۱۳ همتا» on ONE lifetime session, because copilot.py:288 derives `thin` from the same peer-only `low_n` plus `group.n < 8`. Scale is worse than the report implies rather than better: /api/meta lists all 343 merchants down to sessions=1, 262 of them (76%) below the 500-session bar their own peers must clear, and I swept all 187 merchants with <100 lifetime sessions — 187/187 get a non-suppressed peer page with ranked rows, 9 of them at percentile 100 on every shown row. Two small corrections that do not change the verdict: (a) the payload does carry the merchant's own n as `group.me.sessions` (lifetime, not period-scoped), so "the UI cannot warn" is slightly overstated — the UI has the number at PeersPage.tsx:30 and simply ignores it; (b) the quoted empty-state and tooltip copy is literally about peer count («دست‌کم ۵ همتای واقعی»), so this is a violation of the surface's honesty principle rather than a word-for-word contradiction of that one sentence. Severity stays high, not critical: no money is wrong and the rank is arithmetically correct (100% of 11 peers genuinely convert below 1.0); the defect is a missing caveat on a headline claim, on ~54% of the selectable merchant list. confirmed.title: Every axis label on the flagship trend chart reads backwards in Persian
confirmed.location: frontend/src/components/charts.tsx:11 (dir="ltr" on the TrendChart wrapper) — rendered on /#/overview
confirmed.evidence: Measured per-character x-positions of all recharts tick tspans on the live merchant Overview via Range.getBoundingClientRect(). All 16 labels place the number to the LEFT of the Persian word: {"s":"۳۰ میلیارد","order":"LTR (number on the LEFT = wrong for fa)"}, {"s":"۹ تیر","order":"LTR (...)"}, {"s":"۲۵ خرداد", ...} — 15 of 16 flagged, the 16th being a wrapped word-only tspan. The 3x crop confirms the Y axis reads «میلیارد ۳۰ / میلیارد ۱۵ / میلیارد ۷٫۵» and the X axis «تیر ۹ / خرداد ۲۵ / اردیبهشت ۱۹» — month-before-day and unit-before-magnitude, both reversed. I then injected one CSS rule into the live page: `.recharts-cartesian-axis-tick-value, .recharts-cartesian-axis-tick-value tspan { unicode-bidi: plaintext; }` and re-measured: every label flipped to "RTL (correct)", and the crop now reads «۳۰ میلیارد» and «۹ تیر».
confirmed.fix: Add one rule to theme.css: `.recharts-cartesian-axis-tick-value, .recharts-cartesian-axis-tick-value tspan { unicode-bidi: plaintext; }`. `plaintext` resolves each label by its own first strong character, so Persian labels go RTL while the chart geometry keeps the `dir="ltr"` it needs for the `reversed` X axis. Verified working on the live page.
confirmed.verdict: Reproduced exactly, independently, on the live deployment — I could not refute it. `frontend/src/components/charts.tsx:11` really does set `dir="ltr"` on the TrendChart wrapper, and that is the whole cause. In an LTR base paragraph the UBA's rule W7 rewrites the leading Persian digits (U+06F0–U+06F9, class EN) to L because sos=L, N2 then resolves the separating space to the embedding direction L, and only the Arabic word stays at level 1 — so a two-token label like "۳۰ میلیارد" lays out with the number on the LEFT. My Range.getBoundingClientRect() sweep over all 16 recharts tick tspans on https://zarbin-nine.vercel.app/#/overview flagged 15 of 16 as "number on the LEFT" (the 16th is the single-token "۰" tick, and one Y tick, "۲۲٫۵ میلیارد", happens to read correctly only because recharts wraps it onto two lines at width=70, swallowing the space — itself a second, smaller defect visible in the screenshot). The rendered crop confirms it: the Y axis reads «میلیارد ۳۰ / میلیارد ۲۲٫۵ / میلیارد ۱۵ / میلیارد ۷٫۵» and the X axis «تیر ۹ / خرداد ۲۵ / اردیبهشت ۱۹». Injecting the reviewer's exact one-line rule `.recharts-cartesian-axis-tick-value, … tspan { unicode-bidi: plaintext; }` flipped all 16 to "number on the RIGHT" and the crop then reads «۳۰ میلیارد» and «۹ تیر». The finding is also new — grepping docs/EXPERT_REVIEW.md and docs/EXPERT_REVIEW_ISSUES.md for bidi/plaintext/TrendChart turns up nothing on axis-label direction, so this is not a re-report of something already recorded as fixed. Two corrections to the reviewer, neither of which changes the verdict: (1) the IMPACT wording "numbers rendered in the wrong order" overstates — the digits *within* each numeral are correct (۳۰ is thirty, ۲۲٫۵ is 22.5, not ۰۳/۵٫۲۲); what flips is the token order (unit-vs-magnitude, month-vs-day), so no number is misread as a different number and nothing on the traceability/engine claim is touched. (2) The sibling `dir="ltr"` blocks in the same file (charts.tsx:94 `.pct-track`, :113 `.wf-track`) are unaffected — they contain no text, so the fix is correctly scoped to line 11. Severity: I keep it at high, not medium. It is presentation-only and misleads nobody about a value, which argues down; but it is every axis label on the hero visual of the primary merchant page, in the product's only language, it is what a native Persian judge sees first, and the fix is one CSS declaration — that is squarely "a real defect a serious team would fix before shipping."

confirmed.title: Grounding guard is permutation-blind: the LLM can rebind engine numbers to the wrong metric and pass as "grounded" — observed live as median→mean
confirmed.evidence: 8 serial live calls to https://zarbin-nine.vercel.app/api/copilot/polish?m=M156&q=<نرخ تبدیل من چقدر است؟>: 7 accepted, and 3 of those 7 replaced the engine's «میانهٔ مبلغ هر پرداخت موفق ۴۱٫۴ میلیون ریال» (MEDIAN) with «میانگین»/«متوسط» (MEAN), e.g. «... متوسط مبلغ هر پرداخت موفق ۴۱٫۴ ...», each returned as {'source':'llm','grounded':True,'fallback':False,'quality_flags':[]}. Ground truth from DuckDB: SELECT avg(amount), median(amount) FROM sessions WHERE merchant_key='M156' AND session_status='Verified' → mean 63,953,119.4 vs median 41,410,040.0 (ratio 1.544) — the published "average" is 35% low. Reproduced offline: grounding_failure('میانگین مبلغ هر پرداخت موفق ۴۱٫۴ میلیون ریال است.', DET) → None. Same hole, worse payload, on the priorities answer: swapping 61.8B and 147.3B yields «مبلغ واقعی در انتظار تعیین تکلیف (برآورد نیست): ۱۴۷٫۳ میلیارد ریال» — a 2.4x overstatement of REAL settled money explicitly labelled "not an estimate" — grounding_failure(...) → None. Also None for: verified↔sessions swap (۳۰٬۵۰۸ جلسه ثبت شد و ۵۵٬۹۴۰ به تایید رسید), GMV↔median swap (میانهٔ ... ۱٫۹۵ هزار میلیارد ریال), percentile 60→5 (شما در صدک ۵ از ۶۰ همتا), verified-count→customer-count. Script: pipeline/_panel/attack.py.
confirmed.fix: Trace numbers with their anchor, not alone. In _values, capture the nearest preceding content-word span (the metric label) alongside (unit, value), and in _traces require the LLM's anchor to share at least one non-stopword with the deterministic anchor for the matched value. As a cheap first cut that closes the observed live case immediately, treat statistic-name words (میانه/میانگین/متوسط/صدک/مجموع/بیشینه) like _POLARITY_MARKERS: flag any that the LLM uses and the engine did not.
confirmed.verdict: I could not refute this; it reproduces both offline and live, and I found two aggravating details the reviewer missed plus three corrections to their report. (1) OFFLINE — `grounding_failure` returns None for every permutation I threw at it against the real M156 deterministic text: median relabelled as mean («میانگین/متوسط مبلغ هر پرداخت موفق ۴۱٫۴ میلیون ریال»), sessions↔verified swap, GMV↔median swap, verified-count-as-customers, and the priorities swap of ۶۱٫۸ میلیارد (paid_unverified, explicitly labelled «برآورد نیست» = real settled money) with ۱۴۷٫۳ میلیارد (an opportunity estimate). The mechanism is exactly as claimed: `_values()` builds a list of (unit_family, magnitude) pairs and `_traces()` asks only "does some deterministic pair have this family and this magnitude" — membership in a multiset, never binding to the metric the number belongs to. (2) LIVE — 8 serial calls to /api/copilot/polish?m=M156 with «نرخ تبدیل من چقدر است؟»: 7 accepted as source=llm, grounded=true, fallback=false, quality_flags=[], model nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free; ONE of them (p1) replaced the engine's «میانهٔ» with «میانگین» — an unprompted, merchant-facing median-published-as-mean. Ground truth from DuckDB on data/marts/sessions.parquet (M156, Verified, n=30508): mean 63,953,119.4 vs median 41,410,040.0, so the published "average ticket" is 35% below the real average. Three corrections to the reviewer, none of which rescue the code: (a) their rate is overstated ~3.5x — I saw 1/8 (12.5%), not 3/7 (43%); (b) all the money-swap payloads (61.8B↔147.3B, verified↔sessions, GMV↔median, percentile) are hand-injected strings into grounding_failure(), confirmed None but never observed emitted by a real model, so the "2.4x overstatement of real settled money" is a demonstrated guard hole, not a demonstrated production event; (c) they failed to cite ZB-039 ("Guard is unit- and metric-blind… wrong metric passes", recorded ✅ fixed in main) — this finding is its unfixed residual, and per the panel rules I verified it: the ZB-039 examples now correctly REJECT (cross-family «۲۳٬۸۰۱ درصد»/«۵۴٫۵ مشتری» → ungrounded_number; rial→toman → ungrounded_number), while every SAME-family permutation still passes, so the unit-family fix closed only the cross-family half. Two things the reviewer understated: the merchant UI auto-calls polish on every answer and swaps in the LLM text whenever source==="llm" (frontend/src/components/Copilot.tsx:76-84) — no opt-in — under a footer that reads «اعداد هرگز توسط هوش مصنوعی ساخته نمی‌شوند»; and the answer's own evidence array for this question carries only gmv and conv, with no median-ticket metric at all, so there is no evidence-drawer counterweight telling the merchant 41.4M was a median. Also worth a ticket: run p2 silently DROPPED the median sentence entirely and was still accepted as grounded (omission, not permutation). tests/test_grounding_calibration.py contains zero permutation cases, and its FAITHFUL list explicitly requires "reordered clauses" and "shortened" to pass — which is why binding is hard to add, not why it is unnecessary. Severity critical stands under the stated rubric: wrong money reached a merchant, live, carrying grounded:true and the AI chip.

confirmed.evidence:
grounding_failure('', DET) → None and grounding_failure(' \n ', DET) → None (no forbidden match, length ok, no numbers to trace, no markers, _unsupported_sentence finds no content words, novel list empty). End-to-end with a fake provider returning '': gateway.explain(...) → source=llm grounded=True fallback=False flags=[] and answer_fa=''. Reachable: OpenRouterProvider.complete (provider.py:83) returns content.strip() without an emptiness check, so a content-filtered or immediately-truncated completion yields ''. Client: `a: better.source === "llm" ? better : x.a` — no non-empty guard — and the render is `

{t.a!.answer_fa}

`. Scripts: pipeline/_panel/attack.py, pipeline/_panel/e2e.py.
confirmed.fix: One line at the top of grounding_failure: `if not llm_text.strip(): return "empty_output"`. Belt-and-braces: make the client swap conditional on `better.source === "llm" && better.answer_fa.trim()`.
confirmed.verdict:
I could not refute this one — it reproduces exactly as written, at the exact lines cited. `grounding_failure('')` returns None, and `copilot.answer(..., provider=)` yields `source='llm', grounded=True, fallback=False, quality_flags=[], answer_fa=''`, which Copilot.tsx:81 swaps in unconditionally and line 139 renders as an empty `

` under the «با کمک هوش مصنوعی» and confidence chips. Telemetry is emitted with success=True and grounded=True, so AI-Ops does score it as a clean LLM win. The polish path is live in production (3 of 6 probes returned source=llm and were swapped in), and there is no client-side timeout to save it. Three corrections to the write-up, none of which kill it. (a) It is not new: the previous panel logged this verbatim as **ZB-097 (medium, "not verified")**, including the same `answer_fa=''` evidence; the reviewer re-reported it without disclosing that, which the brief required. It is genuinely still open, so the finding stands — but as "unfixed known issue", not "discovery". (b) "Silent data loss" is overstated: the loss is conspicuous, not silent — the merchant sees a blank bubble and can re-ask, and the guard's money-safety property is untouched (no wrong number can ever be shown, only a missing one). One blank per rare event also will not move an AI-Ops aggregate, so "shows it as a win" is technically true and practically negligible. (c) Reachability is asserted, not measured: the reviewer used a fake provider, and 6 live calls to the real free model produced zero empty completions, so the rate is unknown. What keeps it at high rather than medium is something the reviewer missed: the same missing guard also accepts a mid-sentence truncation — `grounding_failure('در این بازه ۵۵٬۹۴۰ جلسهٔ پرداخت ثبت شد و', det)` → None — which is strictly more likely than an exact-empty completion (AI_MAX_TOKENS=600, and a hybrid-reasoning model's reasoning tokens eat that budget), reads as a finished answer rather than an obvious blank, and lands on both merchant and ops surfaces. Zero tests cover any of it, and the fix is one line (`if not comp.text.strip() or len(comp.text) < k*len(det): fallback with a bad_output flag`) — the root-cause place being gateway.grounding_failure, so both callers get it.

refuted.title: The two largest deploy artifacts are outside git and outside CI; the CDN-served SPA is an unverified manual copy of the tracked one
refuted.why: The mechanical facts reproduce exactly — public/ is gitignored, untracked, 1.1 MB, a hand-made copy of the tracked zarin/static, and CI touches neither it nor data/ — but both stated impacts, which are the load-bearing part of a "high", do not survive contact with the deployment. (a) The "second engineer" scenario is self-refuting: public/ is untracked, so a second engineer's clone has NO public/ at all, and every path public/ does not contain falls through to the function's catch-all over the git-tracked zarin/static (proved live: /nonexistent-route and /merchant/M156 both return Server-Timing and the current bundle). Their deploy is therefore correct, just CDN-cold for `/`; the only tree that can hold a stale public/ is the maintainer's own, whose recipe step 2 (`rm -rf public && cp -r`) is idempotent. (b) Even in the maintainer's stale case the divergence is loud, not silent: `/` would serve the old shell from the CDN while `/merchant/M156` serves the new one from the function — two app versions in one deployment, visible on the first deep link, not something "local testing passes on". (c) The marts half is a mischaracterisation: .vercelignore exists to stop the .gitignore fallback deleting marts that ARE in the working tree; a clone has no marts for any ignore file to save, because the anonymised payments dataset is deliberately uncommitted (committing it would be the worse finding, and CI runs on fixtures for exactly that reason). "Clone + vercel deploy --prod 500s" is skipping step 1 of a documented 4-step recipe whose §5 already warns that git-connected deploys ship no marts, and db.py fails with a named instruction rather than a bare 500. What remains is real but small: there is no guard making the copy unskippable. The lazy fix is one line in frontend/package.json — `"build": "tsc --noEmit && vite build && rm -rf ../public && cp -r ../zarin/static ../public"` — which also puts it under the existing CI frontend job. Nothing here is wrong money, a security hole, or a false claim; nothing is currently broken (verified by md5/etag against the live CDN, not by reading the recipe). Severity low, medium at the very outside — not high.
refuted.ran:
All commands run at C:\Users\pro\OneDrive\Desktop\zarinpal (HEAD d17de22).

refuted.title: Peer percentile has no floor on the merchant's own sample size: n=1 yields a green "better than 100% of 13 peers" verdict on the live site
refuted.why: The mechanism reproduces exactly and I could not break it: zarin/peers.py floors the peer side twice (pool sessions>=500, per-peer HAVING sum(sessions)>=100) and defines low_n as len(vals)<8 — a PEER count — while nothing reads the merchant's own denominator, so live /api/peers?m=M164 (own sessions=1) returns four rows at percentile 100 with suppressed:false and low_n:false, and PeersPage.tsx:57 paints them chip-good with no caution. My independent sweep of all 343 merchants replicated the reviewer's counts to the digit (1687 published rows, 556 from <30-own-session merchants, 522 coloured, 362 at exactly 0/100, 187 merchants under 100 own sessions, median 69, min 1), and I found an extra propagation they missed: copilot.answer('M164','مقایسه با همتایان') returns confidence="high" alongside «صدک ۱۰۰ از ۱۳ همتا». What is overstated is the severity and the blast radius. No money is wrong: the money-facing path already has the own-side floor the peers path lacks — insights.py gates every card on ctx.me["sessions"] < MIN_SESSIONS_INSIGHT (100) at lines 246/256/267/308/415, and insights.generate('M164',...) returns zero cards, zero rial. The percentile is arithmetically correct and honestly described in the registry ("exact rank among peers ÷ n peers", not a distributional assumption); the defect is a missing uncertainty gate on a display surface, not a false number, which is the "high" band rather than "critical" under the stated rubric. The impact line "the majority of the merchant population" also does not survive: at the coin-flip threshold it is 116/343 merchants (34%) with <30 own sessions receiving a coloured chip, and 28 (8%) at n<=3; the 55% figure uses <100 own sessions, where a percentile is coarse but not a coin flip. Those 187 thin merchants carry 1,253 of 2,062,839 period sessions — 0.06% of the platform, i.e. the dormant tail. Genuine defect, correctly located, fixable with one own-n floor inside benchmarks() that covers PeersPage, copilot and the evidence drawer at once — but high, not critical.

refuted.title: The advertised peer-matching rule is silently discarded for 82% of merchants; the fallback pool's median peer is 45× larger and converts 30pp better
refuted.why: Every descriptive number in this finding reproduces exactly — the level split (281/43/19), the 81-merchant pool, the 45.2x/666.7x size ratios, the 0.5896-vs-0.2872 conversion split, pearson +0.3089, and M136's {cat, g:0, tk:0} params live. But each causal claim built on them is wrong, and the two that matter run backwards. (a) The bias mechanism does not exist: every peer at every level is drawn from the same sessions>=500 pool, and inside that pool pearson(log sessions, conv) is -0.0164 (spearman -0.028, conv flat across size quartiles at .575/.652/.586/.575). The +0.309 the finding cites is a pool-vs-outside artefact created by the >=500 floor, which applies identically at scale+ticket — the fallback does not introduce it. (b) The direct counterfactual refutes the baseline claim: across the 85 merchants where both peer definitions yield >=3 rated peers, the category fallback's peer p50 conversion is on average 0.6pp LOWER (median delta exactly 0.0000, higher in only 34/85). (c) The money claim inverts: recomputing the whole opportunity book under a forced tight band vs forced category gives category/tight = 0.9513 (33.9e9 vs 35.6e9 IRR), larger in 9 cards and smaller in 12 — the fallback deflates the book by ~5%. (d) The named "mechanism amplifier" contributes exactly zero rials: all 62 zero-gmv merchants have verified=0 (zero revenue in six months, so gmv_per_day=0 is the truth and a x1/4..x4 band around zero is undefined by construction), and `_apply_gmv_cap` demotes every rial estimate for a zero-GMV merchant to a zero-impact alert — I measured 15 such demotions. (e) The IRR is immaterial and misattributed: sub-500-session merchants account for 7.97e9 of a 5.06e11 book, 1.58%. (f) "Silently discarded" is false three times over — the cascade is documented in docs/ANALYTICS.md:47-48 directly beneath the very rule quoted as "the documented rule", in the peers.py docstring, returned as `group.level`/`group.rule_fa`, exposed with `where_sql`+`params` in the evidence drawer, and rendered verbatim by PeersPage.tsx:27; live M136 states "all active merchants in your category (at least 500 sessions)", not the tight band. The fallback's actual effect is coverage, not inflation: 144 cards exist only under it versus 3 only under the tight band, because `_gap_card` needs >=5 rated peers and the tight band rarely clears it — deleting the fallback would blank the peers page for four merchants in five without de-biasing anything, and the suppression floor (MIN_PEERS=5), the `low_n` flag below 8, and the Persian small-pool caution already fence the residual noise. What genuinely survives is one line of copy: the static PeersPage subtitle "مقایسه فقط با پذیرندگانی که واقعاً شبیه شما هستند — نه میانگین کل بازار" does not soften when `level === "category"`, so for a merchant whose peers are 45x larger it oversells what the category level delivers, sitting awkwardly beside the `rule_fa` two lines below that tells the truth. That is a one-line frontend copy fix, not a statistics defect — no wrong money, no false claim, no misleading number.

refuted.title: Operator/Control Center surface has no real authentication (self-mintable ops token behind a fake OTP login)
refuted.why: The MECHANISM reproduces exactly and I do not dispute it: anonymous POST /api/auth/session?scope=ops mints a valid ops token, GET /api/admin/platform with it returns 200 (343 merchants, gmv 5,165,464,690,799) while no token returns 403, auth_session performs no credential check, and Login.tsx's OTP form never validates the 5 digits. I mark this refuted because the IMPACT is materially overstated and the severity is inflated. The headline exposure the reviewer claims ("platform metrics, per-merchant rankings/GMV") is ALREADY 100% public with no token at all: /api/meta is unauthenticated and returns all 343 merchants with per-merchant gmv/sessions/verified, and summing it reproduces the "ops-gated" platform KPIs byte-for-byte (343 / 2,062,839 / 1,025,655 / 5,165,464,690,799), with the same GMV ranking /api/admin/merchants returns. The token's incremental disclosure is only obs/ai-ops telemetry (2 requests, $0 cost, no models) and data-source status (GA4 not_configured); a regex sweep for keys/secrets/paths/emails across all six ops payloads (18,083 bytes) found nothing. A working lockdown also already exists: with ZARIN_ADMIN_TOKEN set and REQUIRE_AUTH off, a self-minted ops token gets 401 — the deploy simply does not set the env var. The posture is deliberate and documented in-code (Login.tsx:12-13 "Demo gate: no auth backend in the challenge build, so any 5-digit code proceeds") and in memory.md:134 ("Single-tenant; no auth/RBAC enforced"), and the reviewer's own impact paragraph concedes this is an intentional demo rather than a breach — which is not a "high". Two things the reviewer MISSED that keep this at medium rather than low: (1) ZARIN_REQUIRE_AUTH=1, the documented hardening flag, actively REOPENS the bypass — with ZARIN_ADMIN_TOKEN set, flipping REQUIRE_AUTH on moves self-minted-ops from 401 to 200, because _admin_guard's "if REQUIRE_AUTH and _ops_session(...)" accepts a self-mintable token; turning the security knob on weakens the admin gate; (2) docs/EXPERT_REVIEW.md:353 records ZB-019 as "fixed in main" when the fix only moved the gate from 200-without-header to 403-then-mint-then-200, so the review record overstates the remediation. Those two deserve tickets. The UI copy ("log in with your ZarinPal account", no demo disclaimer on screen) is a fair but cosmetic complaint. Net: real defect, wrong severity, wrong impact — the operator surface guards data that is already anonymously public.

The MECHANISM is real and I reproduced it exactly, twice — but the finding as written is overstated on three of its four load-bearing claims, and one half of its own title is not a defect at all.

CONFIRMED. `zarin/ai/gateway.py:286-297` sets `base.fallback=True` and attaches the real `comp.latency_ms/cost_usd/model/provider` while leaving `base.source=="deterministic"`. `zarin/ai/telemetry.py:53-54` then builds the latency population as `llm=[e for e in ev if e.get("source")=="llm"]`, so every guard-rejected call is dropped from p50/p95/p99. My synthetic repro emitted the claimed dashboard row byte-for-byte (llm_requests=2, deterministic=98, fallback=8, fallback_rate=0.08, p95=900). Better, I reproduced it LIVE on one warm instance: 8 real polish calls to nvidia/nemotron (6 guard-rejected, 2 accepted), after which /api/admin/ai-ops reported `llm_requests=2, fallback=6, p95=6638` — while the rejected calls I watched come back carried latencies of 6277/6675/7223/8294/10174/**18680** ms. `models` shows `count: 2` for a model that was actually invoked 8 times. The UI tooltip in `frontend/src/ops/OpsAI.tsx:42` is the sharpest proof: it promises «۹۵٪ درخواست‌های مدل سریع‌تر از این زمان پاسخ گرفته‌اند» ("95% of MODEL requests answered faster than this") next to p95=6638, when 6 of 8 model calls were slower. That claim is simply false, and it is the part of this finding that deserves a ticket. The reviewer also missed a gap that strengthens their own case: the provider_error branch (gateway.py:279-283) fires before any latency is captured, so an OPENROUTER_TIMEOUT (config.py:42, 20s) records `latency_ms=None` and contributes nothing to p95 either — the single worst case is invisible on any code path.

REFUTED / OVERSTATED. (1) "Understates the LLM fallback rate ~10x" is not a defect. `fallback_rate` is documented at `zarin/ops_copilot.py:39` as «fallback ÷ کل درخواست‌ها» (fallback ÷ ALL requests) and the UI bar is labelled «سهم پاسخ‌هایی که مدل زبانی کنار گذاشته شد» — share of all ANSWERS. It computes exactly what it says. "True rate = 0.80" is a different metric (per-LLM-attempt) the product never claims to show. A diluted denominator is weak metric design, not a miscomputation. (2) Both headline magnitudes are artifacts of the reviewer's own fixture — they chose 8 rejects at 17000ms, so "~19x" and "~10x" are properties of their test data, not measurements of the system. Live the real magnitudes are 2.8x (18680 vs 6638) and 3.25x. (3) Their live evidence does not reproduce: I got `fallback=0, llm_requests=0, p95=null` on a cold instance with no `/api/copilot/polish` row in /api/admin/performance at all — telemetry is per-serverless-instance and ephemeral, so `fallback=14/llm_requests=3` and `p95=4873 vs 15585.2` are unverifiable by anyone. (Their reasoning there was sounder than I expected — I measured provider lat=18680 against Server-Timing app;dur=18734.3, only 54ms of scope difference — but the numbers themselves are gone.) (4) "Hides the slowest calls entirely… an operator would never escalate" is contradicted by the same panel: `hallucination_risk=6` is computed over ALL events (telemetry.py:59), is correct, and renders directly beneath a stat reading «با مدل زبانی: ۲». Six risk events against two LLM requests is a glaring on-screen contradiction. The failure COUNT is honest and visible; it is the LATENCY and the unit cost that are wrong. (5) `cost_per_request` (5x overstated in my repro: 0.05 vs 0.01) errs toward alarm, not complacency, and is currently inert on a free model (cost_usd=0.0) — it mildly undercuts their own "would never escalate" thesis.

Severity: medium, not high. No money is wrong, no security boundary is touched, this is an internal operator panel, and its failure counters are accurate. What is genuinely broken is one percentile and one unit-cost divisor — worth a ticket (the honest fix is a `llm_attempted` flag, or selecting on `latency_ms is not None` instead of `source=="llm"`), not a ship blocker.

refuted.title: Response cache returns merchant data before the merchant auth dependency runs
refuted.why: The MECHANISM reproduces exactly — byte-for-byte, including the reviewer's own 22,378-byte figure — and I am not disputing it: `cache.middleware` (zarin/cache.py:94-107) keys on `path?query` only and returns from the `_get(key)` branch before `call_next`, so `Depends(_merchant_scope)` (zarin/api.py:121) never runs on a HIT; with ZARIN_REQUIRE_AUTH=1 a cold anonymous GET /api/overview?m=M156 is 401, and after one authenticated request the same anonymous GET is 200/HIT with an identical body, as is a request bearing an M18-scoped token, as is `Authorization: Bearer garbage`. The code should be fixed (two lines: skip the response cache and the `public, s-maxage` header whenever REQUIRE_AUTH is on, or fold the bearer claim into the key). But BOTH load-bearing halves of the write-up are wrong, and they are what carries it to "critical". (1) The premise "the product's own documented production posture (ZARIN_REQUIRE_AUTH=1, which is what the prod-shaped migration path calls for)" is false: the string `ZARIN_REQUIRE_AUTH` appears in zero files under docs/ and in no deploy config (vercel.json, Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml set only DATA_PATH/HOST). The documented production path is docs/DEPLOYMENT_SPEC.md:73-75 — "AuthN: none (single-tenant) → **OIDC**; sessions", "AuthZ → **RBAC** … tenant-scoped queries enforced at the boundary", "Multi-tenancy → tenant id on every row/query; isolation tests" — i.e. replace this layer, not flip this flag. Every mention of the flag (config.py:23-26, auth.py:11-15, api.py:124-128, api.py:228) explicitly calls it an opt-in demo seam. (2) The impact "the merchant isolation control is a no-op for every cached path" misattributes the cause. `POST /api/auth/session` (api.py:226-243) mints a signed 12-hour token for ANY merchant_key with zero credentials — no password, no OTP, no identity check anywhere in the file; `_check_merchant()` only asserts the merchant exists. I verified that with REQUIRE_AUTH=1 and a self-minted token an attacker gets 200 on a COLD cache (`cold overview, self-minted token: 200 MISS 22378`), on the route the cache deliberately excludes (`/api/copilot: 200`), and on the operator surface (`/api/admin/platform: 200` with a self-minted ops token). So under the flag the isolation control is a no-op on every path, cached or not, and the cache grants no access that is not already one unauthenticated POST away — it cannot be "what makes isolation a no-op" when the flag was never on. What survives is real but smaller than claimed: a cache whose key omits the identity dimension, plus `public, s-maxage=31536000` on a per-merchant body (RFC 9111 does permit a shared cache to store an Authorization-bearing request's response when `public`/`s-maxage` are present, so that sub-claim is mechanically right — the live edge does store these: `X-Vercel-Cache: HIT`, `Age: 200`, though it rewrites the downstream header to `public, max-age=60`). Zero exposure in the shipped configuration, zero marginal exposure in the flagged one, no deploy or doc that turns it on: that is a ticket, not a critical. I'd call it medium — high only under the counterfactual where someone gates token issuance properly and leaves cache.py untouched, which is exactly why it deserves the two-line fix now.

refuted.title: Throughput decreases under concurrency; p99 rises 18.7x from 4 to 32 in-flight requests
refuted.why: The measured *shape* half-reproduces, but every load-bearing claim built on top of it is wrong. (1) The named location is a red herring. I ran the identical app with the DuckDB budget set to 1, 4 (default) and 16 threads: conc=4/conc=32 throughput was 35/29, 33/25, 33/26 rps respectively — indistinguishable, and threads=1 was marginally the *best* with the lowest CPU per request (77 ms vs 107 ms at threads=16). `PRAGMA threads=4` at zarin/db.py:35 is not the ceiling. Corroborating this: the server process never exceeded ~45% of 8 logical cores at any concurrency, so it is not even CPU-saturating. (2) The real limiter is the single Python process, and it is a flag away. Same code, same pragma, `uvicorn --workers 4`: conc=8 gave 94 rps / p99 131 ms versus 28 rps / p99 598 ms on one worker; conc=32 gave 70 rps / p99 1542 ms versus 28 rps / p99 2920 ms — 3.3x throughput, 1.9x better tail. And the "peak then decline" curve persists at 3x the level with 4 workers (94 → 70 rps), so it is generic oversubscription, not a defect in db.py. (3) "Hard ceiling near 20 req/s" is a product of the driver, not the system. Every endpoint tested is in `cache.CACHEABLE` and ships `s-maxage=31536000`; the cache-busting parameter no real client sends defeats both layers. Without it, the same single-worker server did 68 → 370 → 530 → 625 → **636 rps** at conc 1/4/8/16/32 with p99 = 86 ms at conc=32, monotonically increasing, zero degradation — 23x the claimed ceiling, on a key space of 343 merchants against a 512-entry LRU. (4) The Vercel impact statement is contradicted by the live deployment: `/api/overview?m=M156` returns `X-Vercel-Cache: HIT, Age: 790` — the lambda is not invoked at all; and when I forced 32 concurrent cache-busted requests at the live origin, `Server-Timing: app;dur` stayed flat at 45 ms p50 / 155 ms p99, i.e. the origin never queued. That header does capture in-process queueing (locally at conc=32 srv_p50 1099 ms tracked client p50 1108 ms), so its flatness live is evidence, not an artifact. The 24.5 s-vs-maxDuration:60 worry does not describe the deployed system. (5) "p99 rises 18.7x from 4 to 32" is Little's Law, not a finding: 8x the in-flight requests at fixed throughput must produce ≥8x the wait. (6) "44 OS threads while only 4 DuckDB workers exist" reproduces (43 measured) but is Starlette's default 40-worker anyio pool for sync `def` routes — framework default, unrelated to DuckDB, and already recorded as ZB-072 (MEDIUM). (7) Novelty is thin: this is the residual of ZB-002 (docs/EXPERT_REVIEW_ISSUES.md:34, "Process-wide RLock serializes every DuckDB query — hard concurrency ceiling", measured 6.5 req/s, marked fixed). The fix took the uncached single-process ceiling from 6.5 to ~30 req/s; re-grading the leftover saturation curve as a new `high` is regression-by-relabelling. What genuinely survives is one sentence of the original: there is no admission control — `zarin/__main__.py:26` calls `uvicorn.run(...)` with no `--limit-concurrency` and no `--workers`. That is real, matters only on the self-hosted path, is fixed by two flags, and is `low`. Also worth noting the claimed absolute numbers are ~2x pessimistic against my hardware (their conc=1 7.5 rps vs my 12.6; their peak 19.6 vs my 29–43 across six runs, with 25.7–43.4 run-to-run spread at conc=4 alone — enough noise that "every step beyond 4 is slower" is not a supportable statement, and their own 10x dataset peaks at conc=8, contradicting it).

refuted.title: No DuckDB memory limit and a spill directory on a read-only filesystem; peak RSS is 11x at 10x data
refuted.why: Partly reproduces, but the two things that make it "high" are both wrong. CONFIRMED: `zarin/db.py:35` sets only `PRAGMA threads=4`; a fresh connection reports `memory_limit`=25.0 GiB and `temp_directory`=`.tmp`, and grep over the repo finds no other pragma. Memory does grow with data under in-process concurrency — my 32-concurrent mixed-endpoint load peaked at 240 MB on the 1x marts and 2,271 MB on a 10x mart set I built, worse than the reviewer's 154/1,720 MB. Setting `memory_limit='512MB'` cuts that 10x peak to 739 MB (fits a 1 GB function) for ~1.9x wall time, so the one-line fix works and deserves a ticket. REFUTED, in four places. (1) "11x at 10x data" is presented as amplification; it is linear — 10x rows, 9.5x memory in my run, 11.2x in theirs. (2) The spill half of the finding is inert and contradicts the memory half: at the 25 GiB default DuckDB never reaches its budget, so it never spills — after a full `/api/customers` at 1x and 10x plus three concurrent load runs, `.tmp` was never created in cwd. The "one escape valve on a read-only path" describes a branch that the finding's own configuration makes unreachable; the same one-line fix that sets the limit would set the temp dir. (3) "Hard OOM kill with no diagnostic" is wrong in both branches: with a limit low enough to force spilling and an uncreatable temp dir, DuckDB raises an explicit `IOException: IO Error: Failed to create directory "<path>"`, and a real container OOM on Vercel/Lambda is logged as `Runtime exited with error: signal: killed` with a Max Memory Used line. Forced spilling to a writable dir also just *worked* — the whole-platform 20.6M-row customers query completed inside a 143 MiB budget. (4) The failure is not reachable in the shipped configuration. Concurrency inside the process is bounded by Starlette's 40-worker anyio threadpool, so 1x peaked at 308 MB under 96 concurrent — only 1.28x the 32-concurrent figure; it cannot climb to 1 GB at the shipped dataset no matter the arrival rate. And the 10x scenario cannot deploy on the target the finding cites: my 10x marts are 275 MB of ZSTD-15 parquet (artificially compressible — duplicated rows dictionary-encode far better than real data, so a realistic 10x is 400-630 MB), `vercel.json` ships `data/marts` inside the function, and Vercel's unzipped serverless limit is 250 MB. At 10x this fails at build time, not at OOM time, and the answer is not a pragma. One unresolved point the finding also did not check: the 25 GiB it quotes came from the reviewer's 31 GiB dev host. Vercel Python functions run on Firecracker microVMs whose guest kernel reports MemTotal ≈ the configured function memory, so DuckDB's 80%-of-physical default in production is plausibly ~80% of the function allowance, i.e. roughly the back-pressure the finding says is absent. No endpoint exposes `current_setting`, so I could not settle it live — but the finding asserts the opposite without evidence. Minor: the location is db.py:35; 33-34 are a comment. Medium, not high: a real "SET memory_limit from the container allowance" ticket, not a production-blocking OOM.

refuted.title: Two of the five /api/customers queries ignore the selected date window, so narrowing the period cannot reduce the cost
refuted.why: The mechanical observation is true and I reproduced its cost curve — interval and cohorts genuinely have no date predicate, they are ~40% of the endpoint at 1x, and they scale near-linearly with a merchant's history (12→62→289 ms from 1x to 10x to 30x). Everything after that is wrong. This is not an oversight the team missed: analytics.py:215 documents it in a comment, and the product surfaces it to the user twice — the cohort section sub-line says "computed over the whole data window, not just the selected period" and the median-interval tile carries a «کل بازه» chip. More importantly, the implied fix is a correctness regression, not an optimisation: I applied PERIOD_SQL to both queries on a 1-week window and the cohort grid collapsed from a 6-month retention matrix to one k=0 cell, and the median inter-purchase gap went from 27.7 days (n=6707) to 1.0 day (n=31) — a merchant-facing number wrong by 27x. A lifetime-retention metric that changed when you narrowed the viewport would be the defect. The impact framing is also overstated in two ways: "no user action can reduce" is the intended semantics (these two answers must not move with the picker, and the other three queries do scale — 30.3→18.6 and 22.0→10.3 ms), and "per uncached call" quietly hides that /api/customers is in CACHEABLE with s-maxage=31536000 plus a 512-entry process LRU over immutable marts, so a cold compute happens once per (merchant, window) per deployment, not per user. At real current scale the cold live cost is 171-196 ms server-side, not a "600 ms floor". What survives is a genuine but modest note: cohorts and interval are the only per-merchant aggregates not precomputed into a mart the way merchant_daily is, so the window-independent portion of this one endpoint grows with per-merchant history and would want a cohort mart before ~10x. That is a medium-at-most ticket dressed up as a high-severity scaling defect, and the specific remedy the finding implies would break two numbers.

(a) The headline is factually wrong: M31 is not the largest merchant. It is #2 by sessions and outside the top six by money; the actual largest, M156 (1,951B IRR, 17x M31, and demo entry #1 — the real first-click path), does NOT exhibit this, publishing a clean 98.2B–196.4B band with capped=false. (b) "No interval" is true, but "no caveat / the most confident presentation" is not: InsightCard.tsx:92 fires a chip-warn «سقف واقع‌بینانه» on precisely these cards, and insights.py:143-145 replaces the impact label with "this stage loses more than half of payments — fix the infrastructure first", so the card never tells the merchant it can recover that money; the reviewer's framed impact ("a merchant is told it can recover an amount equal to every rial it earned") does not survive reading the rendered label. (c) It is not new: docs/EXPERT_REVIEW_ISSUES.md:811 is ZB-060 with the same title, location, M265 evidence and recommended fix, graded MEDIUM, plus ZB-058 for the confidence-forcing half; commit 1eb964e closed only ZB-001..044+120, so these were never claimed fixed and re-reporting them at HIGH inflates a known MEDIUM. Scope also argues down: 9 of 343 merchants (2.6%) have a flat capped rial card at rank 1, and no money is wrong anywhere — GMV, sessions and rates are all correct; what is defective is the collapse of the [0.5, 0.75, 1.0] scenario band into one clamped figure and the broken-branch override that forces confidence="high" (ZB-058), i.e. confidence-in-the-problem being fed into a field that means confidence-in-the-estimate. One point where the reviewer was too soft rather than too hard: the copilot path (`format_impact`) prints «۱۱۴٫۵ میلیارد ریال» with no cap caveat at all, so the chip does not protect the chat surface — that is the strongest version of this finding and it is still a medium.

So "the capability to gate exists and was simply not applied to the merchant surface" is the opposite of what the code does — it is applied and enforced, and the live deploy runs the documented demo default (zarin/config.py:26). The gap between the live URL and a tenanted deploy is one Vercel env var, not the "single hard blocker to a pilot". (2) IT IS ZB-001 + ZB-030, both marked "fixed in main" in docs/EXPERT_REVIEW_ISSUES.md:20 and :424 — the brief required disclosing that and showing the fix is still absent; the reviewer did neither, and the fix is not absent. The source is already pseudonymous at source: `data/other_challenge_data.csv.gz` header is session_key,try_seq,terminal_key,merchant_key(M145),category_id,...,payer_card_key — no merchant name, no card, no customer identifier anywhere in the API.
