WHAT DOES SURVIVE, and it is sharper than what was reported: the tenancy fix is inert on the nine cacheable routes, because `zarin/cache.py:94-107` middleware runs BEFORE the route dependency and keys only on `path?query` — no identity in the key. refuted.title: At the weekly cadence the product claims for itself, 79% of merchants get an empty feed
refuted.why: The arithmetic reproduces exactly — every figure cited is correct — but the finding is refuted on its premise, its population, its characterisation of the evidence, and its novelty. (a) The 79% headline measures a 7-day window the product does not offer: ctx.tsx exposes only all/90d/30d with `all` as default, api.py defaults to the full dataset range, and `rg` finds no 7-day window anywhere in frontend, backend or docs. Worse, `_card_change_alert` returns None below 28 days by construction, so the single most common card is structurally excluded from the reviewer's window — a large part of the 538→98 card collapse is the engine correctly refusing to halve a 7-day window, not the engine going silent. (b) 160 of the 270 "empty feed" merchants at 7d had ZERO payment sessions in the window and 92 more had 1-29; only 5 had ≥100. At 30d, 92 of 172 had zero sessions and the whole zero-card set holds 1.35% of six-month GMV. Returning nothing to a merchant who transacted nothing is `insights.py:663` working, and it is the product's own stated principle («عدد مشکوک/کم‌نمونه حذف می‌شود»). (c) On the default window the six ≥100-session zero-card merchants are the platform's best converters — M97 at 77.6% conversion on 12,753 sessions, M100 at 82.3% — so "the engine can't produce insight for them" inverts what is actually happening. (d) gmv_change is not "an alert with impact 0": it carries risk_gmv=479.7B rial, an impact_label_fa naming that rial change, and a decomposed driver attribution; impact_low/high=0 is the deliberate encoding for "not a recoverable-money estimate", which is precisely the discipline product claim 5 demands, and calling the answer to the product's own headline question («چه تغییر کرد؟ چرا؟») filler misreads the field. (e) The IMPACT paragraph invents its premise — there is no subscription, pricing, retention or engagement claim anywhere in PRODUCT.md, README.md or PLATFORM_BOOK.md to underwrite. (f) Decisively, this is ZB-003 ("37% of merchants see an empty dashboard", business lens) re-reported without acknowledgement, which the record marks ✅ fixed — and the fix worked: 126/343 (37%) then, 75/343 (22%) now on the same window, a 40% reduction. The prior verifier had already made the same "'empty dashboard' is inaccurate" correction I found independently and had already downgraded it critical→high. The brief required verifying and saying so before re-reporting a fixed finding; instead the direction of travel was reported backwards. One genuinely new, small thing survives: Overview.tsx:94 has no zero-sessions guard, so a merchant with 0 transactions in the window is told «این خودش نشانه خوبی است» — tone-deaf, though the KPI strip directly above already shows 0/0. That is polish, not the claimed defect.

refuted.title: The most prominent money figures in the product carry no currency unit at all
refuted.why: The mechanism reproduces exactly — `rial(v, false)` is shipped bare on the copilot landing glance, on every insight-card money headline and range, and (a surface the reviewer missed) in the evidence drawer's «مبلغ» column — but the finding as written is overstated in its headline, wrong in its central impact example, and inflated in severity. The title says "the most prominent money figures in the product carry no currency unit at all"; that is false. The most prominent money figures are the Overview KPI tiles, and `Overview.tsx:52,67` render `{rial(k.gmv,false)}ریال` — verified in the deployed bundle as `ce(a.gmv,!1)` followed by `{className:"u",children:"ریال"}`. The Ops platform KPIs do the same, the funnel table puts the unit in the column header, and the chart tooltip uses `rial(v)` with the unit. The real pattern is a convention — state the unit once per container — applied in five containers and forgotten in three, which is a consistency bug, not an absent unit. The impact paragraph then picks the one example that refutes itself: "the number they are most likely to act on (paid-unverified) is the one shown bare on both the landing strip and the card." On `/#/overview` that figure is rendered *above* the cards, in a callout, as «۹۱۲ پرداخت به مبلغ ۶۱٫۸ میلیارد ریال» (`Overview.tsx:77`, `rial()` with unit), and the copilot's own answer for that intent returns «مجموع ۶۱٫۸ میلیارد ریال». So the merchant acting on paid-unverified sees the unit in both places they would actually act from; only a user who never scrolls past the chat landing strip sees it unlabelled. "The product contradicts itself" is likewise inflated — it omits a unit in some places and states it in others; it never states a *different* unit, and `تومان` has zero occurrences in `frontend/src`, so the product never invites the toman read by name. Finally this is neither new nor a regression: both call sites predate the reviewed commit 75de6bb, and the previous panel already logged the same underlying risk as ZB-085 (rial-only, no on-screen currency note, no toman toggle), still unfixed. The residue is genuine and worth a ticket — a one-token fix (drop `, false`, or add the `ریال` the sibling components already use) on three surfaces, one of which is the default landing screen — which is medium, not high: it never produces a wrong number, never asserts a wrong unit, and every neighbouring rendering of the same figure names ریال.

refuted.title: Tooltips never open on tap or click — on a phone the entire plain-language glossary is unreachable
refuted.why: The observable reproduces exactly — mobile tap 0/0/0/0, desktop click 0/0/0/0, hover 1 — so the tooltip genuinely does not stay open on a pointer press, and the code comment at Tooltip.tsx:45 ("Opens on hover, keyboard focus, and tap") is false. But the finding is wrong in its cause and overstated in its impact and severity, on three independently checked points. (a) The stated mechanism — "onFocus fires first and calls open(), then onClick reads the fresh box and closes" — is not the cause. My event log shows `mouseenter` is what opens it (Chrome fires the compat mouse sequence on a tap), and tap #2 fires NO focus event at all yet still ends at 0 pops. So the culprit is `onMouseEnter={open}` colliding with the `onClick` toggle; deleting or reordering `onFocus` fixes nothing, and neither does deleting `onMouseEnter` alone (focus would then open and click would still close). The real fix is the toggle itself — gate hover-open behind `matchMedia('(hover: hover)')`, or ignore a click that lands in the same gesture that just opened the box. (b) "the entire plain-language glossary is unreachable / the product's answer to 'what does نرخ تبدیل / کوهورت / پنجک mean?' exists and cannot be opened" is false for two of its own three examples and mitigated for the third: «کوهورت» is explained in always-visible Section `sub` text directly under the heading (CustomersPage.tsx:62); «پنجک» has no `<Term>` anywhere in the codebase — there is nothing to open, so the tooltip bug is not why it is unglossed; and «نرخ تبدیل» has an adjacent `.ev-btn` measuring 24x44 that I tapped successfully on the same mobile context, yielding a Persian definition, formula, grain, sample size and SQL. The same holds on the funnel, where the evidence definition spells out NoAttempt and its distinction from a bank error — i.e. the exact substance of TIPS.noattempt. Every page carrying `<Term>` also carries an `EvBtn`, so the register that is lost on touch is the friendly three-part gloss, not all explanation. (c) The tap-target line cites 44px as "the touch minimum"; 44px is WCAG 2.5.5 Target Size (Enhanced), AAA. The AA bar is 2.5.8 at 24x24, which carries an explicit exception for targets inline in a block of text — which is precisely what a `.term > .lbl` is. At 19-21px they sit under 24 but land in the exemption; and the actual controls next to them are already a deliberate 24x44 (see the ui.tsx EvBtn comment about a "real ≥24×24 icon hit area"). Also note the desktop half of the evidence is a non-impact: hover returns 1, so a mouse user reads the tip and the click merely toggles it shut, which is defensible. So: real defect, worth a ticket, wrong diagnosis, and the touch-user harm is a degraded explanation register rather than an unreachable one. Medium, not high — no wrong money, no security, nothing misleading; and it is adjacent to but genuinely not recorded by ZB-091, which the reviewer got right.

refuted.title: Signed deltas paint the +/− on the wrong side of the digits — and the test file claims otherwise
refuted.why: The core mechanism reproduces — I could not refute it — but two load-bearing supporting claims are wrong, and the severity is inflated. CONFIRMED: `pp()` (frontend/src/fmt.ts:32) and the Waterfall label (frontend/src/components/charts.tsx:122) hand-concatenate a bare U+2212, and `zarin/fa.py` emits a bare ASCII U+002D — none of the three prefixes U+200E. Node's own ICU disagrees: `Intl.NumberFormat('fa-IR',{signDisplay:'always'}).format(-1.4)` = `200e 2212 6f1 66b 6f4`, i.e. CLDR deliberately inserts the LRM for fa. Working the UBA by hand on "−۱٫۴ واحد" under `<html dir="rtl">` (frontend/index.html:2, and `.num` in theme.css:62 sets only tabular-nums, no direction): U+2212 is bidi class ES, W4 does not apply (no preceding EN), W6 turns it to ON, N1 puts it between sos=R and an EN-treated-as-R so it resolves R at level 1 while the digits sit at level 2 — L2 reordering yields visual "دحاو ۱٫۴−", sign to the right. Same derivation with the LRM prepended: W7 flips both ENs to L, N1 makes the sign L, the whole numeric run lands at level 2 and renders "دحاو ‎−۱٫۴". So the reviewer's per-glyph measurement is right, and fmt.test.ts:12 "Identical on screen in RTL" is measurably false. REFUTED — claim 1: "renders inconsistently with the Intl-formatted numbers sitting in the same card" is false in the shipped product. I checked all ~60 call sites of `rial()`/`pct()`/`faNum()` in frontend/src: every one receives a count, a GMV, a rate or a share (structurally non-negative), or is explicitly wrapped in `Math.abs()` — ChangesPage.tsx:65 `rial(Math.abs(d.delta_gmv))`/`pct(Math.abs(rel))`, Overview.tsx:22 `pct(Math.abs(d))`, CopilotPage.tsx:20 `pct(Math.abs(dp))`, charts.tsx:122 `rial(Math.abs(it.value))`. The LRM-emitting negative branch of Intl is exercised only by fmt.test.ts:69/96/133. Nothing on screen anywhere in the product carries an LRM'd sign, so there is no mixed rendering in one card; every sign the product draws is hand-prefixed and every one lands on the same side. The real inconsistency is between the shipped UI and a unit test's expectation, which is a smaller thing than claimed. REFUTED — claim 2: "affects every signed value in the product" overstates the blast radius. There are exactly three sign-emitting sites: fmt.ts:32 (`pp()`, used in precisely one place, ChangesPage.tsx:111), charts.tsx:122, and fa.py-generated sentences. The period-over-period deltas a merchant actually reads fastest — the ones the impact statement invokes — are arrow-coded, not sign-coded (Overview.tsx:22 and CopilotPage.tsx:20 use ▲/▼ with `Math.abs()`), so they are untouched. Both affected UI sites also redundantly encode sign as colour (`v >= 0 ? "var(--good)" : "var(--bad)"` at ChangesPage.tsx:111 and charts.tsx:121), so no reader loses the sign, only its position. SEVERITY: high is wrong. No number is wrong, no sign is lost, no money is misstated; the glyph sits where an unmarked bidi run puts it by default, which is what a large share of Persian web content looks like. It is a genuine non-CLDR i18n defect with a one-character fix (prefix U+200E in `pp()`, charts.tsx:122 and fa.py, or wrap in `<bdi>`), plus a test comment that misleads the next engineer. That is a ticket, not a ship blocker — medium, consistent with this panel's own calibration where purely visual defects with no data/correctness impact were downgraded from high to medium (docs/EXPERT_REVIEW_ISSUES.md:477).

refuted.title: Copilot gives a screen-reader user no announcement for 9.3 seconds and then an unreliable one (4.1.3)
refuted.why: The structural core reproduces exactly and I confirm it: before asking there are zero live regions (`[]`); the pending bubble sits in no live region (`{"pend":true,…,"lr":[]}`); and the `aria-live="polite"` node first appears in the DOM in the same React commit as its content, which is the classic non-announcing pattern. But the two claims that turned this into a *new*, *high* finding are both wrong. (a) The "measured 9,286 ms" of silence does not exist. In two real-Chrome runs the deterministic answer landed at 679 ms and 1,295 ms; `Server-Timing` for `/api/copilot` is 6–200 ms. The 9.2 s figure is `/api/copilot/polish` (`app;dur=8769.7`, wall 9.2326 s) — the LLM rephrasing pass that runs *after* the answer is already on screen and that the pending bubble never covers. The reviewer attributed polish latency to the answer path, so the IMPACT paragraph's "hear nothing for ~9 s" is inflated ~10x; the real gap is under a second. (b) The "perverse" mechanism is wrong. The «در حال روان‌تر کردن بیان…» chip is *not* a later mutation of an already-present region: Copilot.tsx:70 and :77 are two setStates in one synchronous continuation, so React 18 auto-batching co-inserts the chip with the answer — proven in both runs, where the chip is already present in the very first snapshot that contains the answer. And in both runs polish never replaced the text (source chip stayed «محاسبه قطعی از داده شما»), so there was no announceable text mutation at all; the only later change is the chip's *removal*, which default `aria-relevant="additions text"` does not announce. So "the rephrasing is spoken but the original answer is not" did not happen. (c) The finding is not new: ZB-093 is an open, unfixed MEDIUM with the identical file:line, the identical "created in the same render as its content" mechanism, the identical pending-bubble observation and the identical 4.1.3 citation. The only fresh material offered was the measurement, and the measurement is wrong. Note also that the reviewer's evidence is DOM queries, not a screen reader — "which NVDA/JAWS do not announce" is asserted, not tested, exactly as in ZB-093, so it adds no verification either. Verdict: the defect is real and worth fixing (a persistent `<div aria-live="polite" aria-busy={pending}>` wrapper around `.chat` is a ~3-line change), but it is a correctly-classified MEDIUM that is already on the books, dressed up with a 10x-overstated latency number and an incorrect mechanism.

refuted.title: Metric tooltips fail 1.4.13 on both Dismissible and Hoverable
refuted.why: Half of this finding is disproven and its headline impact sentence is factually false. I drove the live deployment with the same tool the reviewer used (real CDP `Input.dispatchMouseEvent` against Chrome 151 headless on https://zarbin-nine.vercel.app, merchant session seeded via `sessionStorage.zb_ws`) and reproduced their hover numbers exactly — tooltip 197px tall, 300px wide, `pointerEvents:"none"`, 10px gap, `activeElement = BODY`, and Escape does nothing on the hover-only path. But the claim "cannot be dismissed without moving the pointer" is wrong: I dispatched a real `mousePressed`/`mouseReleased` pair at the identical coordinate (929.09, 283.99) — the pointer never moved a single pixel — and the tooltip closed (`open:false`). That is literally the mechanism SC 1.4.13 Dismissible asks for ("a mechanism … to dismiss the additional content without moving pointer hover"). The reviewer stopped at Escape and never tried the click, even though `onClick={() => (box ? close() : open())}` is on the same line range they cite. Both keyboard paths also pass Dismissible: after a click the span holds focus and Escape closes it, and after a pure `\.focus()` (Tab-equivalent) the tooltip opens and Escape closes it. So Dismissible is REFUTED and only Hoverable survives. Hoverable does genuinely fail — panning the pointer onto the tooltip centre closes it — but the reviewer's named root cause is also wrong. `.tip-pop { pointer-events: none }` (theme.css:379) is not what breaks it: I forced `pointerEvents='auto'` on the live popover and it still vanished on pan. The actual cause is `Tooltip.tsx:39` `Math.min(window.innerHeight - 230, r.bottom + 10)` — a 10px dead gap — combined with `onMouseLeave={close}` on the trigger; the pointer dies 2px below the trigger, inside the gap, before it can ever reach the tooltip. Their recommended fix (drop pointer-events:none) would therefore not fix it. Two secondary overstatements: "affects all 21 TIPS definitions" conflates the dictionary size with rendered instances — I counted per route: overview 4, funnel 8, peers 2, customers 3, changes 4, quality 0, copilot 4, and it is one shared component, one defect, not 21. And the escalation to HIGH is unearned: ZB-091 already records this at MEDIUM, the reviewer's justification for going higher was "both Dismissible and Hoverable", and one of those two is disproven. What remains is exactly the MEDIUM already on the books. One point does go the reviewer's way: I checked whether the 1.4.13 Dismissible carve-out for content that "does not obscure other content" applies, and it does not — `elementsFromPoint` under the tooltip centre returns `BUTTON.prompt-card` with real text, so the popover does cover an interactive element. That makes 1.4.13 applicable, it just does not make the finding correct as written.
